Additionally, the Office of Energy Dominance Financing within the U.S. Department of Energy has formally announced the successful financial closure of a loan, which may reach up to $1.9 billion, designated for NextEra Energy. This financial support aims to facilitate the restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center, located in Linn County, Iowa. Furthermore, this strategic investment endeavors to reactivate Iowa's sole nuclear power facility, thereby promoting the energy dominance agenda articulated by President Trump, along with the Executive Order focused on reinvigorating the nuclear industrial base.

It is worth noting that U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly remarked that President Trump has established an ambitious trajectory aimed at restoring American leadership in the nuclear sector. He emphasized that the recommissioning of the Duane Arnold Nuclear Plant signifies another significant advancement in the nation’s nuclear renaissance. Moreover, the reintegration of 615 megawatts of dependable baseload electricity generation is expected to contribute to the reduction of electricity expenses while simultaneously supporting thousands of employment opportunities for American workers. This Administration is proactively pursuing a holistic nuclear strategy, which includes the restart of existing reactors, the augmentation of output from the current nuclear fleet, and the acceleration of new construction initiatives to establish a power system that is abundant, affordable, and reliable—these are deemed essential for the prosperity and reindustrialization of America.

In essence, the recommissioning of the Duane Arnold Energy Center is projected to reintroduce 615 megawatts of reliable baseload power to the electrical grid, which is sufficient to supply energy to nearly 500,000 residences. This initiative will also assist in addressing the escalating demand for electricity in Iowa and the surrounding region. Additionally, the project is anticipated to generate nearly 1,500 jobs for American workers during the construction phase while sustaining over 450 jobs during the operational phase. Ultimately, these developments reflect an important step toward enhancing the nation’s energy infrastructure and economic stability.

The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing today announced the financial close of a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra Energy to help finance the restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Linn County, Iowa.

WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Energy Dominance Financing (EDF) today announced the financial close of a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra Energy to help finance the restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center in Linn County, Iowa. The investment will bring Iowa's only nuclear power plant back online, advancing President Trump's energy dominance agenda and Executive Order, Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base.

“President Trump has set an ambitious course to restore American nuclear leadership, and the restart of Duane Arnold Nuclear Plant in Iowa marks another step in advancing America’s nuclear renaissance,” said U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy James P. Danly. “Returning 615 megawatts of reliable baseload generation will drive down electricity costs, while supporting thousands of American jobs. This Administration is pursuing a comprehensive nuclear strategy, restarting existing reactors, increasing the output of our nuclear fleet, and accelerating new construction, to build the abundant, affordable, and reliable power system required for American prosperity and reindustrialization.”

Duane Arnold’s restart will add 615 megawatts (MW) of reliable baseload power back on the grid—enough to power nearly 500,000 homes—and help meet growing electricity demand in Iowa and across the region. The project will create nearly 1,500 American jobs during construction and support more than 450 jobs during operations.

title: https://www.energy.gov/articles/energy-department-announces-99-million-21-projects-advance-us-geothermal-energy
input:
It is worth noting that the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) recently announced an investment exceeding $99 million for 21 selected projects aimed at promoting the development of geothermal energy throughout the United States. These projects are expected to conduct field-scale evaluations of advanced geothermal technologies, along with exploration drilling efforts designed to characterize and potentially confirm the presence of promising geothermal resources.

Furthermore, it can be suggested that the leadership of President Trump has played a role in advancing American geothermal innovation, which may unlock the significant domestic energy resources available in the nation. Geothermal energy has the potential to deliver reliable, continuous power, which can assist in meeting the increasing energy demand while also enhancing U.S. energy security.

Notably, DOE Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit remarked that these projects will provide opportunities for American innovators to tap into the expansive geothermal resources located beneath the surface. Under the guidance of President Trump, the advancement of next-generation geothermal technologies can lead to reduced costs, reinforce American energy dominance, and convert more of the abundant domestic geothermal resources into dependable and affordable energy.

In essence, the 21 selected projects will focus on enhancing geothermal development in two significant areas. Specifically, five of these projects will undertake field-scale tests of enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) to validate their technologies in practical settings, while 16 additional projects will engage in exploration drilling to identify and characterize next-generation geothermal resources that may hold promise. Collectively, these initiatives are expected to mitigate technical and development risks, as well as furnish essential information that can support future commercial projects and investments.

Ultimately, the data generated from these initiatives will be made publicly accessible through the DOE's Geothermal Data Repository (GDR), potentially providing industry professionals, researchers, and other stakeholders with valuable insights from the field tests and geothermal exploration activities. By making this information available, the projects may extend their benefits beyond individual sites, thereby aiding in the future development of technology and geothermal exploration across the industry. In summary, these efforts are anticipated to significantly contribute to the advancement of geothermal energy in the United States.

input:
It is worth noting that EDF Director Gregory A. Beard emphasized the potential for a nuclear revival, stating that the Department of Energy is making significant progress. He suggested that the Duane Arnold facility represents an investment that may contribute to the restoration of American leadership in nuclear energy, enhance energy security, and provide the affordable and dependable power that can often support the nation’s future energy needs.

In terms of operational status, it is important to recognize that the Duane Arnold facility ceased operations in 2020. However, with the necessary U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission licensing approvals pending, the restart of the plant may return dependable nuclear power to the electrical grid while also addressing the increasing demand for electricity in Iowa and the broader Midwest region.

Furthermore, the Department of Energy appears to be accelerating efforts to expand American nuclear energy, which may facilitate a restoration of the United States' leadership in this sector. This initiative aims to deliver energy that is both affordable and reliable, thereby benefiting the American populace. Following today's developments, it can be observed that EDF has successfully financed a total of three nuclear plant restarts while completing four concurrent conditional commitments and financial closings during the Trump Administration, thus mobilizing capital to enhance the availability of American energy production. Overall, these efforts may play a crucial role in bolstering the country’s energy landscape.

input:
It is a pleasure to be present with you today. Throughout my professional journey, I have had the opportunity to engage with issues that impact rural communities, particularly in relation to access to financial resources. My experiences at the Federal Reserve have further enhanced my understanding of both the opportunities and challenges faced by rural America, particularly as I have traveled extensively to various rural areas over the past several years.

Notably, these communities tend to encounter numerous difficulties, and they may also face unique obstacles that require adaptable solutions. What has particularly resonated with me is the degree of innovation and creativity that can often be observed in many of these solutions. It appears that we should actively seek to highlight these examples, disseminating successful practices and promoting ideas that may help expand opportunities and bolster economic growth throughout rural America.

For instance, in 2023, I had the chance to journey along the Blues Trail in the Mississippi Delta, traversing the route from Jackson to Memphis. Along this path, I engaged with local leaders and representatives from financial institutions, some of whom are here today, to gain insights into how once-thriving rural railroad towns are adjusting to both enduring and emerging challenges.

In Moorhead, Mississippi, which is often recognized as the location where the Southern crosses the Yellow Dog, I observed how a bank that had faced difficulties in maintaining its branch ultimately decided to donate its building to a community development financial institution, thereby preserving crucial access to banking services for a community that greatly requires this support.

Furthermore, in Clarksdale, Mississippi, I had the opportunity to visit the Travelers Hotel, which underwent redevelopment through the utilization of New Markets Tax Credits. This project now plays a significant role in the revitalization of the Blues tourism sector within that historic community. Overall, these experiences illustrate the importance of innovative approaches in addressing the challenges faced by rural communities.

input:
It is worth noting that recent developments in the Middle East may have influenced the availability and cost of fertilizer supplies. More than one-third of global urea exports tends to transit through the Strait of Hormuz, and interruptions in this route can often result in price increases for this essential fertilizer, which may have risen approximately 55 percent since the beginning of this calendar year. Furthermore, the prices for diesel, which serves as another critical input for agricultural producers, appear to have experienced a rise of about 50 percent over the past year. 

Additionally, the increase in fuel costs can place considerable pressure on cattle farmers situated within rural communities, as it tends to elevate both direct and indirect production expenses. Higher diesel prices may lead to increased costs for operating machinery and transporting livestock, while simultaneously contributing to the escalation of vital inputs, such as fertilizer and feed. In a similar vein, transportation costs throughout the beef supply chain often rise in conjunction with fuel prices, which may result in elevated consumer prices and potential reductions in profit margins for producers. 

Notably, dairy farmers may also face challenges due to rising diesel prices, as fuel is commonly utilized at every stage of milk production and distribution. Given the rapidly evolving situation, it may be premature to predict how prices will fluctuate as events in the Middle East continue to develop. In summary, the interplay between geopolitical events and agricultural costs appears to create a complex landscape for producers and consumers alike.

Prices for diesel, another important input for agricultural producers, rose 50 percent over the past year. Rising fuel prices place significant pressure on cattle farmers in rural communities by increasing both direct and indirect production costs. Higher diesel prices raise expenses for operating equipment and transporting livestock, while also driving up the cost of key inputs like fertilizer and feed. Transportation costs across the beef supply chain also rise with fuel prices, contributing to higher consumer prices and squeezing returns for producers. Similarly, higher diesel prices are burdensome for dairy farmers because fuel is used at every stage of milk production and transport. Given rapidly changing circumstances, it is too early to know the path for prices as events in the Middle East unfold.

Diesel prices, another key cost for farmers, have gone up about 50% in a year. 

Fuel costs can hurt rural cattle farmers. Higher diesel means more money for running machinery and moving animals. It also raises costs for feed and fertilizer. Transport costs in the beef chain go up with fuel prices, leading to higher prices for consumers and lower profits for producers.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/cook20250503a.htm
input: It is a great pleasure to offer congratulations to the James Madison College Class of 2025 at Michigan State University, and it is an honor to address such an inspiring and talented graduating class. Before I begin my remarks to the graduates, I would like to express appreciation to those who helped them reach this point, including parents, grandparents, siblings, aunts and uncles, friends, teachers, and mentors. This highlights the importance of the support network that lifted up the Class of 2025, and I offer both congratulations and thanks to all of those individuals. As the child of a professor and as an MSU professor, I have come to value commencements as important milestones, and it is wonderful to be with you today. The flowers are beginning to bloom in Beal Garden, the lawns around Beaumont Tower are turning the perfect shade of Spartan green, and the ducklings are making their appearance on the Red Cedar. After another chilly winter, the campus is reaching peak beauty just in time for your departure from Michigan State. I am full of optimism about everything that lies ahead of you, and despite any sense of angst you may feel about moving on from Madison, I hope that you are filled with optimism as well. Spring is a time of new beginnings, and you are ready for the next step. Today marks both the completion of a tremendous accomplishment and an exciting new beginning. Some of you may be feeling uncertain, which is natural, while others of you may have detailed plans that you are ready to execute. It is worth noting that if you keep your head down and your eyes fixed only on the map, you may miss unexpected opportunities, since life, like Michigan weather, is going to surprise you. As you leave here, I want you to remain optimistic and to have confidence, because you are ready. Ultimately, this occasion represents both a celebration of your achievement and a reminder to remain open to the possibilities that lie ahead.

input:
Throughout my life, many of my most cherished and fulfilling experiences have revolved around opportunities for service. It is worth noting that my involvement with organizations such as 4-H has played a significant role in shaping my values. The pledge of "Head, Heart, Hands, and Health" embodies a commitment to service and community. My experiences have included serving as a page in the Georgia legislature, interning on Capitol Hill, being a member of the Executive Committee of the American Economic Association (AEA), working at the U.S. Treasury and the White House, leading the AEA Summer Program at Michigan State University, and currently serving on the Federal Reserve Board. Each of these experiences has provided me with invaluable opportunities to apply my knowledge, skills, and time towards efforts that aim to improve the world.

As proud graduates of James Madison University, it is essential to actively seek various avenues to contribute to the greater good throughout your lives. Engaging in public service can often be challenging, yet it consistently offers meaningful and deeply rewarding experiences. This engagement may take many forms, including working in education or government, conducting research to enhance our understanding, developing new technologies, volunteering for nonprofit organizations, or providing mentorship to junior colleagues. There are numerous ways, both substantial and minor, to contribute to the community. Thus, as you proceed through life, it is valuable to consider which paths will enable you to make a positive impact on society.

Ultimately, as graduates and members of the Spartan community, you are stepping into a world characterized by urgent needs and abundant opportunities. As you navigate this new phase, it is beneficial to allow hope to guide your journey. You should remain attentive to your curiosity and value deep knowledge combined with diligent preparation. Additionally, the FOMC reached a decision to revise its consensus statement following the completion of a public review, and that review consisted of three principal elements. Furthermore, Reserve Banks hosted Fed Listens events, the Board hosted a research conference, and a series of policymaker discussions was convened at FOMC meetings this year with the support of staff analysis. Moreover, the changes that were implemented as a result of this review represented a logical progression rather than a change in course, and they were grounded in an ever-evolving understanding of the economy. It is worth noting that four adjustments to the consensus statement will be noted and each will be discussed in turn.

Additionally, the revised consensus statement effected a removal of language emphasizing the effective lower bound as a defining feature of the economic landscape, and it instead states that the monetary policy strategy is designed to promote maximum employment and stable prices across a broad range of economic conditions. Furthermore, this revision, which reflects a move away from the post-financial crisis era of historically low interest rates, tends to make the framework more robust. It is worth noting that at the time of the previous framework review during 2019 and 2020, policymakers were considering an economy that had for many years demonstrated low growth, low inflation, and a very flat Phillips curve, which means that inflation was not very responsive to slack in the economy. Moreover, the overarching concern for central bankers at that time was how to operate when short-term interest rates are near the effective lower bound. In essence, a very different environment is being operated in today, at least in part brought on by the economic consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic, and this shift appears to underscore the broader evolution of the framework.

input: In the present day, the Federal Reserve tends to communicate through a variety of channels, and these can often include speeches by policymakers, press conferences held by Chair Powell, and even the Fed's social media outlets. It is worth noting that clear and ample communication has not always appeared to be a hallmark of the Fed, and this may reflect a gradual shift in institutional practice. Additionally, in the 1990s, cable news outlets would often attempt to spot former Fed Chair Alan Greenspan as he walked into the building on the day of FOMC meetings. Furthermore, commentators would pay careful attention to the size of his briefcase, and the thought was that a bulging briefcase would suggest the Chair was advocating a rate change with documents to convince fellow policymakers. In essence, a light bag, on the contrary, would have signaled that a status quo policy decision was likely, and this interpretation appears to have shaped media coverage at the time. Notably, former Chair Greenspan seemed to value the element of surprise, and in 1987 he famously quipped that if he seemed unduly clear to his audience, they must have misunderstood what he said. That said, during his tenure in later years, he initiated substantial changes in how Fed policymakers communicate with the public, and this can often be seen as a move toward greater transparency. Ultimately, the Fed's communication approach has experienced a gradual evolution from ambiguity toward clearer public engagement.

input:
Building a Framework to Better Support Community Banks

Additionally, after acknowledging the significance of community banks and establishing a clear definition of these institutions, it is critical to identify the guiding principles that should govern their regulation and supervision. The principles that guide this approach are relatively simple and straightforward: the regulatory framework must be tailored to the associated risks, characterized by transparency, and consistently applied across similar institutions. In essence, the integration of these elements can create an opportunity to develop a sustainable regulatory and supervisory framework for community banks in the future.

Furthermore, this conference serves as an ideal platform to encourage discussions that may foster innovative ideas aimed at preserving the viability of community banking for the foreseeable future. While it would be unfeasible to provide an exhaustive plan for a community banking reform agenda within the confines of this speech, I recognize several opportunities that appear to be both promising and essential for consideration.

The Value of Experience 

Moreover, the process of constructing this framework for the future fundamentally begins with the personnel involved, specifically those who are responsible for making long-term decisions. It is essential to consider how we approach our responsibilities in this regard. We should emphasize successful examples from the past while also reflecting on the considerable amount of work that still lies ahead.

It is worth noting that Congress designated one seat on the Federal Reserve Board specifically for an individual who possesses demonstrated primary experience in either working within or supervising community banks. Although Congress did not specify any additional responsibilities linked to this particular seat on the Board, the establishment of this role serves as an implicit recognition of the value that such experience can contribute to the Board's various functions, particularly in the realm of bank regulation and supervision. In summary, the thoughtful integration of experience and principles can substantively enhance the regulatory environment for community banks.

input:
Additionally, these protections have served the public well, and administrations from both parties have respected them over time. It is worth noting that if any administration finds a way to remove Fed officials over policy differences, then future administrations will likely do so as well. Furthermore, the public would lose faith that the central bank will make decisions based only on what is best for all Americans. In essence, the credibility of the Fed would be lost as a result of such actions. Notably, that credibility enables the Fed to support a strong and stable economy for the benefit of American families and businesses. Our credibility has been built and sustained over many decades, and we have a duty to safeguard that priceless asset for our fellow citizens and for generations to come.

As Americans, we are motivated by the belief that freedom and democracy greatly enhance human fulfillment. The work to preserve and strengthen our own democracy can be noisy, frustrating, and, at times, embattled. Partisan political differences are normal, and indeed essential, in a thriving democracy. However, we ought to be united in our commitment to the higher principles that define our nation. Chief among them is respect for the rule of law. As John Adams wrote, ours is "a government of laws and not of men."

Furthermore, our public institutions carry us forward through change, and they embody our commitment to freedom, democracy, and service of the public good. The philosopher Edmund Burke warned that democratic institutions take much time, effort, and patience to build but can be torn down all too quickly. It is essential that we preserve what is good about these institutions, even as we strive to improve them.

While we will have political differences, at the end of the day, we all love this wonderful country, and want what is best for it and for our fellow Americans. Ultimately, these shared commitments and institutions remain essential to our continued success as a nation.

It is worth noting that community banks ought to be subject to rigorous supervisory oversight; however, this oversight must correspond to their relatively smaller size, less complex business activities, and the limited risks they may pose to the financial stability of the United States. Furthermore, this objective can be achieved by establishing a distinct oversight program for community banks that is separate from those intended for larger and regional financial institutions, thereby allowing examiners to concentrate specifically on the risks and activities pertinent to small banks. This approach would also diminish the inclination to apply standards and expectations originally designed for larger, more complex institutions to community banks.

Additionally, in order to avoid ambiguity, it is beneficial to provide clarity regarding the identification of material financial risks within the supervisory process. This identification does not suggest an exclusive focus on merely checking compliance boxes while reviewing processes, procedures, and documentation, irrespective of the actual assessment of risk. Moreover, it does not imply neglecting other critical components of the established supervisory program.

As noted in the supervisory operating principles, an emphasis on material financial risks necessitates that examiners employ reasoned judgment in prioritizing issues throughout each phase of the examination process. This prioritization commences with the focus outlined in the pre-examination letter, continues through the scope of work during the examination, and involves distinguishing between findings that warrant formal attention and those that may be resolved through less formal avenues. The operating principles explicitly mention supervisory observations for matters that do not constitute violations but may still be documented in the examination report. Ultimately, this approach seeks to enhance the effectiveness of the supervisory process while ensuring that community banks are evaluated in a manner that is appropriate for their specific context.

This could be accomplished by separating the community bank oversight program from those designed for larger and regional banks, focusing examiner attention on small bank risks and activities. This would also eliminate the temptation to "push down" standards and expectations to community banks, that were designed for larger and more complex institutions.

Material Financial Risk To avoid confusion, it may also be helpful to clarify what is meant by identifying material financial risks in the supervisory process. It does not mean focusing primarily on checking boxes in reviewing processes, procedures, and documentation, regardless of the assessment of risk. It also does not mean ignoring other aspects of the established supervisory program.

As the supervisory operating principles note, focusing on material financial risks requires examiners to use reasoned judgment to prioritize through every stage of an examination. This begins with targeting in the pre-examination letter, the examination's scope of work, and differentiating between findings that meet the threshold of a matter requiring attention, and those that can be addressed through less formal means. The operating principles specifically reference supervisory observations for those matters that do not rise to the level of a violation but may be included in an examination report.

A separate oversight plan for community banks would help examiners focus on the risks and activities specific to small banks. This would also stop the tendency to use rules made for bigger, more complex banks on smaller ones.

To avoid confusion, it's important to clearly define what counts as a major financial risk in supervision. This doesn't mean just checking off boxes while looking at processes and papers, no matter what the real risk is. It also doesn't mean ignoring other important parts of the supervision program.

The supervisory principles say that focusing on major risks means examiners should use good judgment to decide what's important at each step of the exam. This starts with the pre-exam letter, continues through the exam's scope, and helps tell which findings need formal action and which can be handled another way. The principles also mention noting observations that aren't violations but still matter. This way, the supervision process is better, and community banks are assessed in a way that fits their own situation.

I wish to express my gratitude to President Nagel and the Bundesbank for the opportunity to engage in this meeting today. It is indeed a pleasure to be present. I value the chance to communicate with groups of young individuals such as this one. Having spent a significant portion of my career in academia as both a professor and university administrator, I appreciate the return to those foundational experiences today. It is my intention to ensure that there is ample time for your inquiries. However, I would like to begin by discussing a subject that has frequently occupied my thoughts, which I believe may also resonate with many of you: artificial intelligence, often referred to as AI.

It is notable that when I interact with students, consumers, or professionals, discussions regarding AI tend to emerge quite rapidly. This trend is understandable, as one does not even need to engage a chatbot to recognize its relevance. AI appears to have the capacity to significantly alter both our work environments and our daily lives, and it may also exert a considerable influence on the economy. Today, I intend to address the swift progression of AI and share my perspective on this technology by analyzing it through the framework of the dual mandate assigned to the Federal Reserve by the U.S. Congress. This mandate directs America’s central bank to strive for maximum employment and maintain price stability. I will outline the potential impacts that AI may have on both aspects of this mandate. Lastly, I will provide a brief update on my economic outlook before I turn the floor over to your questions. In conclusion, I am looking forward to our discussion and the insights it may yield.

But I would like to start by speaking with you about a topic that's been on my mind, and I bet it has been on many of yours: artificial intelligence (AI).

Today, I will talk about AI's rapid growth and how I approach thinking about AI by examining it through the lens of the dual mandate given to the Federal Reserve by the U.S. Congress. That mandate instructs America's central bank to pursue maximum employment and price stability. I will describe the effects that AI may have on both sides of that mandate. Finally, I will briefly update you on my economic outlook before turning to your questions.

When I talk to students, consumers, or professionals, AI comes up quickly. It’s obvious even without using a chatbot. AI has the potential to change how we work, how we live, and how the economy functions. Today, I’ll talk about how fast AI is developing and share my views on the technology. I’ll look at it through the dual mandate of the Federal Reserve as set by Congress: maximum employment and price stability. I’ll explain how AI might affect both. Then I’ll give a quick update on my economic outlook before opening the floor to your questions. In the end, I’m looking forward to our conversation and the ideas it might generate.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20240930a.htm
input:
In recent months, it is worth noting that there has been some progress in the effort to decelerate the rate of inflation, as monthly measurements have indicated levels lower than those observed during the elevated pace of the initial three months of the year. Furthermore, the twelve-month measure of core personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation, which offers a broader insight than the more volatile higher-frequency measures, has experienced a decline since April; however, it registered at 2.7 percent in August, remaining significantly above the desired 2 percent target. The persistently elevated core inflation appears to reflect ongoing pressures related to housing prices, which may be influenced, at least in part, by limited availability of affordable housing options. Although the progress observed in reducing inflation since April is a positive development, it is essential to recognize that core inflation continues to exceed the Committee's target by an uncomfortable margin.

Additionally, it is important to note that prices remain considerably higher than they were prior to the pandemic, which continues to exert a negative influence on consumer sentiment. Higher prices disproportionately affect lower- and moderate-income households, as these households allocate a significantly greater proportion of their income to essential categories such as food, energy, and housing. Moreover, the price increases in these categories have significantly outpaced the general rate of inflation over the past few years.

Moreover, economic growth has moderated in the earlier part of this year, following stronger performance the previous year. It is notable that private domestic final purchases (PDFP) growth has remained robust, demonstrating a slower decline compared to gross domestic product (GDP), as the slowdown in GDP growth was partially attributable to volatile categories, including net exports, which suggests that the underlying economic growth is stronger than what the GDP figures indicate. Furthermore, PDFP has continued to show solid growth thus far in the third quarter, despite some additional weakening in housing activity, as retail sales have demonstrated further substantial gains during the months of July and August. In summary, while there are indications of progress in addressing inflation and sustaining economic growth, significant challenges remain that warrant continued attention.

The progress in lowering inflation since April is a welcome development, but core inflation is still uncomfortably above the Committee's 2 percent goal.

Prices remain much higher than before the pandemic, which continues to weigh on consumer sentiment. title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/jefferson20241009a.htm
input:
It is worth noting that the tragic loss of life, destruction, and damage caused by Hurricane Helene in North Carolina and the surrounding region is deeply saddening. My thoughts extend to the individuals and communities impacted by this disaster. Furthermore, the Federal Reserve, along with various federal and state financial regulatory agencies, is collaborating with banks and credit unions in the affected areas to ensure they can continue to meet the financial service needs of their communities.

Additionally, I shared my historical perspective on the discount window at Davidson College yesterday. In 1913, when the Federal Reserve was established, the discount window served as the primary instrument for providing the nation with a safer, more flexible, and more stable monetary and financial system. More than a century later, the discount window remains integral in supporting the liquidity and stability of the banking system, as well as the effective implementation of monetary policy.

In essence, today I would like to examine how the discount window has undergone evolution in the 21st century, particularly focusing on recent actions taken by the Federal Reserve Board to gather public feedback regarding discount window operations. Before delving into our most recent initiatives, however, it is important to review several significant episodes in the history of the discount window that have shaped its current state. Ultimately, this overview will provide valuable context for understanding the ongoing developments in this area.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/jefferson20251003a.htm
input:
The data available from both government and private-sector sources suggests that labor supply and demand are experiencing a simultaneous slowdown, as indicated by the ratio of job openings to unemployed individuals seeking employment. A few years prior, the number of available jobs significantly outnumbered the unemployment level; however, this situation has returned to a more balanced state over the past year. Recent data released earlier this week indicates that the unemployment level has slightly surpassed the number of job openings during the summer, yet the V/U ratio, which economists use to analyze this dynamic, remains close to 1. Additionally, last week, the Labor Department reported that initial jobless claims continue to show a tendency to remain stable. Furthermore, net immigration into the United States, which serves as an important factor contributing to workforce growth, has experienced a sharp decline, acting as a restraint on a more substantial rise in unemployment.

Furthermore, in addressing the other aspect of our dual mandate, it is noteworthy that inflation has significantly decelerated from the peak levels observed when the economy reopened following pandemic disruptions. Nevertheless, inflation continues to remain somewhat above the 2 percent target that has been established, and the tariffs that have been announced and implemented to date are reflected in the prices of certain goods. Overall, personal consumption expenditures (PCE) prices increased by 2.7 percent over the 12 months concluding in August. Additionally, core PCE inflation, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices, was recorded at 2.9 percent in the month of August.

In examining the drivers of overall price measures, it may be beneficial to analyze the three primary components of core PCE inflation. Currently, core goods prices, which experienced a modest decline last year, have been on the rise, attributed to the effects of tariffs; however, it is important to note that the extent of this increase has been less than what numerous forecasters had anticipated in the spring. Meanwhile, core services inflation, excluding housing, appears to have generally maintained a sideways trend throughout this year, while inflation within the housing sector seems to be gradually declining. This overall analysis highlights the complexities of current economic conditions.

It is worth noting that remaining curious about what others can teach you is essential, and settling for easy answers should be avoided. Furthermore, maintaining a sense of wonder about the world appears to be imperative so that improvements to it can be made. Additionally, curiosity is often described as magical, yet vigilance, practice, and study tend to be required to avoid stagnation and to reach new insights. Ultimately, trusting the guidance of curiosity can often lead to wonderful opportunities.

This leads to a third suggestion for the journey ahead, which is to be persistent. Notably, as Madison graduates, preparation is something you already understand. Furthermore, persistence in your efforts tends to require continual preparation for the next steps, even when the destination remains unknown. In essence, this means grounding what you think and say in deep and informed knowledge, which is acquired through effort and reflection.

Additionally, you are graduating at a unique time in the history of the world. It is worth noting that access to unprecedented quantities of data is now available. Furthermore, tools to gather and analyze these data can often be used to understand and improve the world. Ultimately, learning should be viewed as a lifelong pursuit, and familiarity with new technologies and tools, such as artificial intelligence, should be developed. Notably, these tools should be incorporated into persistent preparation as a companion, not as a substitute, for living an informed, productive, and fulfilling life.

The final guide is a call to service, which is something James Madison students tend to understand well. Furthermore, public service is woven into the culture here. Historically, large numbers of Madison graduates have entered public service jobs immediately after graduation, including with the Peace Corps, Teach for America, nonprofits, and local, state, and federal agencies. In essence, curiosity, persistence, and service together provide a framework for a purposeful journey ahead.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20260107a.htm
input:
In the context of overseeing holding companies, it is important to note that the Federal Reserve is mandated by statute to depend "to the fullest extent possible" on the examinations conducted by the primary state or federal supervisors of subsidiary banks. In practice, this requirement can often impose considerable limitations on the supervisory activities of the Federal Reserve. This situation tends to apply to national banks that are regulated by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) as well as state non-member banks that fall under the purview of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) and a state banking authority.

This statutory requirement is intended to minimize the potential for redundant and burdensome examination processes. Nevertheless, it is essential for the Federal Reserve to possess confidence in the supervisory processes and outcomes of the examinations conducted by the OCC, FDIC, and state banking agencies. Achieving this confidence typically necessitates access to and a comprehensive review of examination reports and related activities. In situations where reliance on such examinations is not feasible or where access to supporting documentation is unavailable, it may be necessary for the Federal Reserve to initiate its own review.

Furthermore, each bank examination culminates in the creation of a report of examination, which serves to document the findings of the examination. This report frequently includes supervisory observations or criticisms, as well as matters requiring attention (MRAs) or matters requiring immediate attention (MRIAs) when such issues are identified during the examination process. Additionally, the report contains the bank's supervisory ratings, which are determined according to the CAMELS rating system.

It is worth noting that the findings from examinations and the inclusion of specific matters within the report can have significant implications for the bank involved. Not only do they guide how banks prioritize their efforts to address identified issues, but the bank's CAMELS rating can also influence its eligibility for favorable treatment regarding banking applications, impact the cost of FDIC insurance premiums, affect the liquidity funding costs, and serve as an indicator of bank management performance for its board of directors. In conclusion, the intricate relationship between examination findings and their consequences highlights the importance of thorough oversight in maintaining the health of financial institutions.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20241002a.htm
input:
When the costs associated with running a bank increase, there tends to be a necessity for making adjustments if the institution hopes to sustain its profitability and, ultimately, its continued operation. This situation may often involve either reducing expenses or increasing fees for banking services.

Furthermore, it is worth considering how the realities of managing a business can inform our current regulatory approaches. This question becomes particularly significant when regulators contemplate the introduction of new or revised rules. Regulators may benefit from consistently evaluating three key areas: first, identifying the specific problem that the new regulation seeks to address; second, assessing the potential costs associated with this regulatory approach; and third, exploring alternative methods that might be available. Before delving into the proposed path forward, it is useful to present an example that illustrates this important concern.

Notably, the final regulations under the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) released in 2023 established new thresholds that categorize banks as "small," "intermediate," or "large." In this context, large banks are defined as those possessing more than $2 billion in assets. It appears that this rulemaking may have represented a missed opportunity to better align the CRA requirements with the realities faced by community banks, as it does not seem to recognize the fundamental distinctions among banks that operate with various balance sheets and business models. In essence, applying the same evaluation criteria to a bank with $2 billion in assets as to a bank with $2 trillion in assets may reflect an oversight regarding the essential differences among financial institutions, as well as the disproportionate costs that these regulations may impose on smaller banks.
human:
When a bank's costs increase, there is, by necessity, a need to make changes if the bank hopes to maintain profitability and ultimately its survival. This usually involves either cutting costs or raising prices on banking services.

How do the realities of operating a business inform our current approach to regulation? The question becomes acutely relevant when regulators consider imposing new or revised regulations. Regulators should always ask (1) what problem does this new regulation solve, (2) what are costs of this approach, and (3) are there alternative approaches? Before discussing the path forward, I would like to note an example that highlights this concern.

The final Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) regulations issued in 2023 established new regulatory thresholds defining "small," "intermediate" and "large" banks, with the last category—large banks—including every bank with more than $2 billion in assets. In my view, this rulemaking represented a missed opportunity to rationalize the requirements of the CRA among community banks, and ignored the fundamental differences among banks with different balance sheets and business models. An approach that applies the same evaluation standards to a bank with $2 billion in assets as it does to a bank with $2 trillion in assets arguably represents a shortcoming in considering the fundamental differences among firms, and the disproportionate costs these standards may impose on the smallest banks.

input:
Furthermore, an illustrative example arises when the rate of inflation is at or below the intended target, while employment levels appear to be near or exceeding estimates of their maximum potential. It is worth noting that, as articulated in the consensus statement of the Federal Open Market Committee, the concept of maximum employment lacks a direct means of measurement and tends to evolve over time, primarily due to factors that are largely non-monetary in nature. Additionally, alterations in the economic structure that are anticipated to persist in the long term may lead to employment levels rising above current assessments of maximum employment, without necessarily exerting upward pressure on inflation beyond the benchmark of 2 percent. The coexistence of low inflation and low unemployment may often signify the presence of favorable supply shocks that are gradually influencing the economy. In such circumstances, in the absence of risks to price stability, the dual mandate objectives may not inherently conflict, and employment levels that appear to exceed their estimated maximum may not necessitate an immediate policy response. This particular dynamic was evident during the latter half of the 1990s, when then-Chairman Alan Greenspan directed the Federal Open Market Committee to refrain from raising interest rates, despite unemployment rates falling below the estimated natural levels, as robust productivity growth facilitated a scenario characterized by both strong output growth and low, decreasing inflation.

In conclusion, it may be beneficial to consider an instance that illustrates the potential tension between our overarching goals, wherein inflation levels are somewhat elevated, the labor market appears weak or is experiencing a decline, and the policy stance has already adopted an accommodative nature. Under such conditions, the need to balance the objectives of maximizing employment and ensuring price stability would suggest maintaining the policy rate at an accommodative level.

Another example is when inflation is at or below target but employment seems near or higher than estimates of its maximum level and the policy stance is close to neutral or accommodative. As described in the FOMC's consensus statement, maximum employment is not directly measurable and evolves over time due to factors that are largely non-monetary. Changes to the underlying structure of the economy that are expected to persist in the longer run may result in employment rising above existing assessments of maximum employment without necessarily generating upward pressure on inflation above 2 percent. The combination of low inflation and low unemployment may reflect positive supply shocks that are working their way through the economy. In that case, absent price-stability risks, the dual-mandate objectives may not necessarily be in tension, and employment that appears stronger than its estimated maximum level may not require a policy response. This dynamic occurred during the second half of the 1990s, when then-Chairman Greenspan led the FOMC to hold off on rate increases even as unemployment moved below the estimated natural rates, as strong productivity growth allowed for a combination of strong output growth and low and falling inflation.

I will conclude this part of the discussion with an example of tension between our goals, with inflation somewhat elevated, a weak or weakening labor market, and a policy stance that is already accommodative. Under these conditions, balancing the maximum-employment and price-stability goals would call for holding the policy rate at an accommodative level.

input:
It is worth noting that recent progress on efforts to lower inflation may have experienced a slowdown, as indicated by rising measures of Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation. Furthermore, on a year-over-year basis, total PCE inflation may have increased to 3.8 percent in April, largely driven by higher gasoline and fuel oil prices. Additionally, core PCE inflation appears to have risen further to 3.3 percent last month, marking a noticeable increase since September. However, other indicators of inflation, which tend to focus on the central tendency of price changes, including the trimmed mean PCE measure, suggest that core inflation may have adjusted closer to 2 percent since last September. It is also important to recognize that price pressures seem to have become increasingly concentrated within a limited range of goods categories, reflecting the effects of tariffs and unique changes in software pricing. When excluding these one-time factors, core PCE inflation may have remained only slightly above 2 percent, indicating a lack of pressures from the labor market and a degree of weakness in market rents.

In addition, it appears to be premature to fully evaluate the extent and duration of the economic impacts stemming from the ongoing conflict in Iran. I tend to maintain an optimistic outlook that, once the conflict is resolved, supply disruptions may lessen, leading to only a temporary effect on PCE inflation and minimal consequences for domestic economic activity. This perspective seems to align with current oil futures prices and the prevailing optimism within financial markets. However, if disruptions were to persist well into the latter part of the year, there may be broader implications for inflation that could emerge. In summary, while there are indications of rising inflation and potential economic impacts from external conflicts, the situation remains fluid and may evolve in various ways.

input:
It is worth noting that the regulators entrusted with the implementation of regulations, supervision, and guidance hold the ultimate responsibility for the decisions related to policy choices. Additionally, this process can often greatly benefit from increased interaction between federal regulators and their counterparts in state bank regulation. By fostering more extensive dialogue with state regulators, it may be possible to enhance proposals during the formulation stage through the sharing of practical, real-world perspectives, which include valuable observations regarding both intended and unintended consequences of reforms. While anticipating unintended consequences presents significant challenges, casting a wide net for diverse viewpoints may lead to more effective, less disruptive, and better-informed policy decisions.

Furthermore, the importance of strengthening coordination between state regulators and the Federal Reserve is paramount. At a recent meeting of the Board's Subcommittee on Smaller Regional and Community Banking, my colleagues and I had the distinct pleasure of welcoming representatives from the Conference of State Bank Supervisors, which included four members of their State Bank Commissioner cohort. During this meeting, we gained first-hand insights into the successes, frustrations, concerns, and potential areas for improvement in the collaboration between state and federal regulators. Such direct conversations are invaluable, as they contribute significantly to building and enhancing these essential intergovernmental relationships.

Moreover, historically, one of the many commendable attributes of the Federal Reserve Board is its structural incentive to collaborate in order to achieve compromise. The governors operate under extended, staggered terms designed to shield them from the immediate influences of political considerations. The Board is composed of seven independent governors who frequently contribute their distinct perspectives on a variety of policy issues. While instances of dissent may attract considerable attention, the Federal Reserve has a long-standing tradition of engaging in thoughtful debates, exchanging views, and ultimately reaching more sustainable compromises on matters of rulemaking. The prevailing consensus on bank regulatory issues is not unexpected, as we work collectively toward the shared objectives of safety, soundness, and financial stability.

input:
When I found myself in a position similar to yours, having recently graduated from Spelman College, I recall experiencing uncertainty regarding what the future may hold for me. I did not envision that I would eventually become a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors or even pursue a career as an economist, as I initially entered Spelman College as a major in physics and philosophy. It was only several years post-graduation, following an unanticipated encounter, that I began to view economics as a viable avenue for my career aspirations. At that particular time, I was furthering my studies in philosophy while residing in Senegal, and I encountered challenges in identifying the appropriate framework through which to investigate the significant questions that inspired and motivated me. Consequently, I made the decision to embark on an adventurous journey: hiking Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania. Fortuitously, during this expedition, I encountered a British economist who, by the conclusion of my trek, persuaded me that economics possesses the necessary tools to engage with the questions I held in high regard. Within a few months, I returned to my home, enrolled in classes to prepare for a Ph.D. in economics, and commenced a trajectory that eventually led me to both Michigan State University and the Federal Reserve.

Today, as you prepare to leave the familiar environment of Case Hall and East Lansing, ready to embark on your next adventure, it is worth noting that I would like to present four guiding principles for you to consider as you navigate the journey that lies ahead: hope, curiosity, persistence, and a steadfast commitment to the principles of public service.

input:
It is worth noting that I expressed support for the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to maintain interest rates at our most recent policy meeting in March. Additionally, while economic growth has remained robust, there are early indications that it may be experiencing a slowdown. Labor market conditions have remained stable through February, and progress regarding inflation has eased; however, the overall outlook appears to be uncertain. These circumstances led me to advocate for maintaining the policy rate at what I consider a moderately restrictive level.

Furthermore, the long-term perspective illustrated by figure 9 indicates that the Federal Open Market Committee responded to the elevated inflationary environment following the pandemic by increasing the policy rate by 5.25 percentage points over a span of approximately 15 months, beginning in March 2022. After maintaining the rate at this restrictive level for more than a year, improvements in inflation allowed a reduction of the policy rate by a full percentage point last year, resulting in the current rate. The experience of inflation moderating toward the 2 percent target without a significant rise in unemployment has been historically unusual, but it is greatly welcomed.

In considering the future trajectory of policy, I intend to continuously evaluate incoming data, the developing economic outlook, and the balance of associated risks. Ultimately, it is important to emphasize that monetary policy does not follow a predetermined path. If economic conditions remain strong and inflation does not progress sustainably toward 2 percent, the present policy restraint may need to be preserved for an extended period. Conversely, should the labor market weaken unexpectedly or inflation decline more rapidly than anticipated, adjustments to policy may be warranted. In my assessment, there is no immediate necessity to expedite further changes to the policy rate. The current policy stance appears to be well positioned to address the risks and uncertainties inherent in fulfilling both aspects of our dual mandate.

Labor market conditions have remained stable through February, and progress on inflation has eased, but the outlook is uncertain. These conditions led me to favor holding the policy rate constant at what I view as a moderately restrictive level.

The longer-term perspective provided by figure 9 shows that the FOMC responded to elevated inflation in the post-pandemic period by raising the policy rate 5-1/4 percentage points over about 15 months, starting in March 2022. Thinking about the future path of policy, I will continue to assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. As we emphasize, monetary policy is not on a preset course. If the economy remains strong and inflation does not continue to move sustainably toward 2 percent, the current policy restraint could be retained for longer. If the labor market were to weaken unexpectedly or inflation were to fall more quickly than anticipated, policy could be eased accordingly. In my view, there is no need to be in a hurry to make further policy rate adjustments. The current policy stance is well positioned to deal with the risks and uncertainties that we face in pursuing both sides of our dual mandate.

input: In the initial phases following the transition to the new facilities, evidence emerged indicating that financially sound depository institutions appeared to demonstrate an increased willingness to engage in borrowing from the discount window. Furthermore, certain research indicated that subsequent to the revisions made to the discount window in 2003, banks tended to borrow more frequently from this source during periods when the federal funds rate experienced a significant increase, compared to previous borrowing patterns. This observation may imply that the restructured discount window was successful in diminishing the hesitation that banks had previously exhibited towards borrowing. Consequently, it can be inferred that the discount window may have become more effective in establishing a ceiling on short-term funding rates, thereby facilitating the implementation of monetary policy and acting as a crucial liquidity tool when circumstances necessitated its use. Ultimately, the findings suggest a positive impact of the changes made to the discount window on the borrowing behavior of banks.

input:
Moreover, closely related to the previously discussed change, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has clarified the approach it intends to adopt regarding monetary policy during those periods when the objectives of employment and inflation may conflict. The revised statement articulates that, in such circumstances, the Committee will implement "a balanced approach in promoting them, taking into account the extent of departures from its goals and the potentially different time horizons over which employment and inflation are projected to return to levels judged consistent with its mandate." This updated language bears a closer resemblance to the original statement issued in 2012 and is consistent with the actions undertaken by the Committee during the period from 2022 to 2024, when significant deviation from the 2 percent inflation target emerged as the predominant concern.

Furthermore, while I have just underscored a series of modifications made to the framework statement, it is also essential to acknowledge the continuity that exists with previous versions of our statement. The document continues to elucidate our interpretation of the mandate provided by Congress and describes the policy framework we believe will most effectively promote maximum employment alongside price stability. Additionally, we maintain that monetary policy must adopt a forward-looking perspective and take into account the time lags inherent in its impact on the economy. It is worth noting that we have never established a numerical goal for employment, as the maximum level of employment is not directly quantifiable and is subject to change over time for reasons not necessarily related to policy initiatives. Likewise, our commitment to a 2 percent inflation objective remains steadfast, as this target plays a critical role in sustaining well-anchored long-term inflation expectations, thereby supporting both dimensions of our dual mandate. Ultimately, we continue to be dedicated to conducting a public review approximately every five years to ensure alignment with our overarching goals.

This passage serves as an introduction to the 2025 community banking research conference. It is worth noting that the speaker expresses regret about not being able to attend in person while also recognizing the significant contributions this conference has made in advancing research related to community banking and its associated issues.

Since its inception in 2013, the conference has effectively synthesized insights from academic research, regulatory bodies, and the banking sector, all aimed at deepening the understanding of the community bank business model. This effort is intended to better inform future policy decisions in the field.

Additionally, the speaker, who has served as the former Kansas state bank commissioner as well as a community banker, expresses appreciation for the conference's objectives. This year, the organizers have once again curated valuable research and developed a program featuring a broad array of perspectives that facilitate discussion and debate among participants.

Furthermore, ensuring the future and viability of the community banking sector remains a critical priority, particularly in light of the recent appointment of the speaker as Vice Chair for Supervision of the Federal Reserve Board by the President.

This particular role, established under the Dodd-Frank Act in 2010, involves the responsibility to develop policy recommendations for the Board regarding the supervision and regulation of depository institution holding companies and other financial entities under its supervision. It also entails overseeing the regulatory compliance of these firms.

Ultimately, the speaker conveys an immense sense of honor and privilege in being entrusted with these significant responsibilities. The speaker looks forward to collaborating with stakeholders across the financial industry to modernize the regulatory and supervisory frameworks, which can foster continued economic growth and innovation within the banking system while enhancing the vital role of community banks.

As the former Kansas state bank commissioner and a community banker, I very much appreciate the goals of this conference. And again this year, the organizers have included valuable research and created a conference program that includes a wide range of perspectives that create an opportunity for discussion and debate.

input:
One significant aspect of our regulatory efforts involves the assurance of consistency and the establishment of a level playing field for institutions that operate internationally. In this context, it is worth noting that, in my capacity as the chair of the Financial Stability Board's Standing Committee on Supervisory and Regulatory Cooperation, we are collaboratively addressing financial stability challenges related to supervisory and regulatory policies. Upon assuming this role and determining our priorities, I identified the critical need to explore sound practices concerning the adoption, utilization, and innovation of artificial intelligence, with the intent to publish our findings and conclusions in a report that solicits stakeholder commentary. Furthermore, the report will offer a comprehensive analysis that underscores the potential advantages and obstacles associated with the application of artificial intelligence, while including fundamental principles and instances of successful AI implementation. In addition to this analysis, we should also reflect on the importance of maintaining consistency in expectations regarding the use of artificial intelligence on an international scale, particularly in relation to cybersecurity and critical infrastructure, especially in situations where international supervisory expectations conflict with those of the home country.

Moreover, our colleagues from the U.S. Treasury and the Securities and Exchange Commission are engaging closely with us on this particular workstream. I anticipate that the consultation draft of this report will be made available in the third quarter, and I strongly encourage all stakeholders to review and provide their feedback on the report upon its release. Ultimately, this ongoing collaboration seeks to enhance our understanding and implementation of regulatory frameworks in the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence.

input:
In the supervisory process, it is essential to maintain focus and avoid distractions from less relevant issues. Additionally, the frequency of supervisory findings related to nonfinancial metrics may be influenced by the time required to address certain issues. This observation raises the question of whether this trend reflects a broader supervisory emphasis that shifts attention from financial risks to non-financial risks and internal processes, a shift that may warrant careful evaluation regarding its appropriateness. Furthermore, it is important to recognize the significant diversity in business models, sizes, and geographical presence among banks, suggesting that uniform standards may not be applicable to every institution. It is crucial to avoid the imposition of uniformity through approaches such as "grading on a curve," as this risk can be heightened during horizontal reviews. Notably, the supervisory findings generated during examinations play a critical role in determining bank ratings, which can subsequently impact various aspects of bank operations, including restrictions on mergers and acquisitions, increased liquidity costs, and the potential diversion of resources from other vital management priorities.

Moreover, guidance issued to banks can often incur costs that may not be immediately apparent or quantifiable. The primary objective of guidance is to enhance clarity for banks while reducing uncertainty and risk during implementation. However, for guidance to effectively achieve its intended purpose, it must be clear, actionable, and responsive to the specific needs of the targeted institutions, particularly community banks. Ultimately, ensuring effective guidance and supervision can contribute to the overall stability and functionality of the banking sector.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20260529a.htm
input:
Payroll employment growth may serve as an indicator of labor market momentum and can often help identify shifts in the path of the unemployment rate. When payroll gains are strong relative to trend labor force growth, they tend to point toward a lower unemployment rate and stronger labor market conditions, whereas weak payroll gains can often point toward a higher unemployment rate. It is worth noting that, because these data can be volatile or unreliable for a variety of reasons, closer attention tends to be paid to average payroll gains over a few months, which helps in understanding whether the labor market is moving closer to or further away from full employment.

Additionally, a multitude of other data is examined, both from the employment report and from other public and private surveys, in order to assess momentum and slack in the labor market. Regarding slack, data on discouraged and marginally attached workers and on involuntary part-time employment can indicate the extent of hidden unemployment and fragile employment. Furthermore, data on wage growth can help assess the relative strength of labor demand and supply, and the ratio of vacancies to unemployment also serves as a measure of labor market tightness. Regarding momentum, the composition of job gains by industry tends to indicate the breadth and depth of employment gains, and the payroll data are adjusted for persistent bias or expected revisions. Notably, indicators of layoffs, such as unemployment insurance claims, can detect early signs of a pickup in unemployment, and data on job openings also provide a signal about the strength of labor demand.

Regarding price stability, or inflation, the FOMC established 2 percent as the inflation goal in 2012, as measured by the annual change in the PCE price index. Consequently, policymakers closely monitor the recent path of total PCE inflation and how it is expected to evolve going forward. Ultimately, these various indicators together provide a broad framework for assessing labor market conditions and the outlook for inflation.

title: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/bowman20260107a.htm
input:
Additionally, community banks, in a manner similar to all banking institutions, are frequently required to obtain regulatory approval in order to engage in certain business activities and mergers, or to undertake new activities. Furthermore, it is worth noting that the process of applying for such regulatory approval appears to have become uncertain, cumbersome, disruptive, and slow in recent years.

Moreover, in some instances, application forms may fail to require a bank to submit the necessary information that is needed in order to evaluate an application properly. Additionally, the application process can often include standards that appear to make little sense when they are applied to community banks, such as the use of restrictive screens for evaluating the competitive effects of mergers in rural and underserved communities.

Furthermore, the process tends to lack specific action timelines that are necessary for business planning purposes. It is worth noting that mergers and acquisitions involve the coordination of a number of time-dependent processes, including transaction closing and staffing related planning, as well as the process of scheduling technology integrations with specialized vendors. In essence, the missing of deadlines can often be costly for the institutions involved, and we are currently working to improve this process by addressing these and other challenges, especially for community banks.

Additionally, I would like to discuss transparency, which I view as a critical element of the regulatory and supervisory processes. Furthermore, transparency in supervisory expectations appears to be just as important as transparency in regulatory requirements, and yet it often tends to receive the least scrutiny and attention.

Moreover, in part, the lack of transparency for supervision may result from information security rules and the manner in which they apply to communication between banks and examiners. It is worth noting that these have been protected from public scrutiny under the broad categorization of confidential supervisory information (CSI). Ultimately, the labeling of information as CSI tends to result in significant restrictions on its disclosure, and banks and bank employees may be subject to criminal penalties if they disclose CSI without regulatory approval, even if doing so would serve beneficial purposes for bank safety and soundness.

Transparency Finally, I would like to discuss transparency, which I see as a critical element of the regulatory and supervisory processes. Transparency in supervisory expectations is just as important as transparency in regulatory requirements, and yet it often receives the least scrutiny and attention.

In part, the lack of transparency for supervision results from information security rules and how they apply to communication between banks and examiners. Community banks, like all banks, often need regulatory approval to do certain business activities, merge with other banks, or start new activities. Recently, getting this approval has become more uncertain, complicated, and slow. Sometimes, the forms they fill out don’t ask for the right information to properly evaluate their applications. Also, some rules in the application process don’t make sense for community banks, like using strict tests to check how mergers affect competition in rural or underserved areas.

The process also doesn’t have clear deadlines that help banks plan their work. Mergers and acquisitions need many time-sensitive steps, like closing the deal, planning staff, and setting up technology with vendors. Missing deadlines can cost a lot. We’re working to fix this by tackling these issues, especially for community banks.

I also want to talk about transparency. I think it’s important for both regulatory and supervisory processes. Transparency in what regulators expect is just as important as transparency in the rules themselves, but it often gets less attention. Part of the problem might be information security rules that limit how banks and examiners communicate. These are called confidential supervisory information (CSI) and are kept private. Banks and employees can face criminal penalties if they share CSI without permission, even if it would help the bank’s safety and soundness.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/08/nist-releases-first-3-finalized-post-quantum-encryption-standards
input:
Furthermore, the standards encompass the computer code for encryption algorithms, the guidelines for their implementation, and their intended applications, representing the culmination of an eight-year initiative overseen by NIST, which has a notable history of encryption development. The agency has mobilized global experts in cryptography to conceptualize, submit, and subsequently assess various cryptographic algorithms that may withstand the challenges posed by quantum computing. While this emerging technology has the potential to bring transformative changes to a variety of fields, including weather forecasting, fundamental physics, and drug design, it also introduces certain risks.

It is worth noting that Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and NIST Director Laurie E. Locascio stated that quantum computing technology has the potential to address some of society's most difficult challenges, and the newly established standards reflect NIST's dedication to preventing any simultaneous threats to our security. The finalized standards can be viewed as the pinnacle of NIST's commitment to protecting our sensitive electronic information.

In essence, encryption plays a crucial role in contemporary digital society by safeguarding vast amounts of electronic information, including email contents, medical records, and photo collections, along with information that is essential for national security. Encrypted data is capable of being transmitted across public computer networks, remaining inaccessible to everyone except the sender and the intended recipient.

Additionally, encryption mechanisms rely on intricate mathematical problems that traditional computers often encounter as exceedingly challenging or beyond their capabilities. However, a sufficiently advanced quantum computer could potentially analyze numerous possible solutions to these problems in a remarkably efficient manner, thereby undermining existing encryption methods. The algorithms standardized by NIST are derived from alternative mathematical challenges that may prove difficult for both traditional and quantum computers to resolve. Overall, this comprehensive approach aims to enhance the security of electronic information in an increasingly complex digital landscape.
human:
The standards — containing the encryption algorithms’ computer code, instructions for how to implement them, and their intended uses — are the result of an eight-year effort managed by NIST, which has a long history of developing encryption. The agency has rallied the world’s cryptography experts to conceive, submit and then evaluate cryptographic algorithms that could resist the assault of quantum computers. The nascent technology could revolutionize fields from weather forecasting to fundamental physics to drug design, but it carries threats as well.

“Quantum computing technology could become a force for solving many of society’s most intractable problems, and the new standards represent NIST’s commitment to ensuring it will not simultaneously disrupt our security,” said Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology and NIST Director Laurie E. Locascio. “These finalized standards are the capstone of NIST’s efforts to safeguard our confidential electronic information.”

Encryption carries a heavy load in modern digitized society. It protects countless electronic secrets, such as the contents of email messages, medical records and photo libraries, as well as information vital to national security.
