title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/07/nist-develops-genetic-material-validating-mpox-tests
input: Additionally, it is worth noting that Victoria Olson, who serves as the CDC’s deputy director of laboratory science and safety, has stated that positive control materials can often be critical for ensuring the reliability of diagnostic tests. Furthermore, she indicated that having a reliable supply of high-quality control material from a trusted source such as NIST may help the agency mount an effective testing program more quickly. In essence, the NIST control material is a liquid solution that contains partial sequences from nine mpox genes, which are strung together into molecules of DNA that are roughly 3,400 base pairs, or letter pairs, long. Notably, the value of the NIST control material does not tend to reside in the DNA itself, which is relatively easy to synthesize. Rather, it appears to reside in NIST’s assurance that each vial of the material contains the same very precisely measured amount of DNA, to a known degree of certainty. To illustrate, each microliter tends to contain 110,000 copies of the DNA strand, plus or minus 10 percent. Additionally, NIST scientists analyzed the DNA in order to ensure that there are no errors in the genetic sequences. Furthermore, they measured the concentration of DNA in the material through the use of a high-precision technique that is called digital PCR. Moreover, they worked with NIST statisticians in order to ensure that each microliter of the material contains the same amount of DNA, within the stated bounds of uncertainty. Scott Jackson, who is the NIST microbial geneticist that led the effort, has said that they do a lot of work in order to make sure that they get those numbers right. On June 22, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced that it would authorize commercial laboratories to conduct mpox tests, which previously were only conducted by a limited number of public laboratories. In addition, commercial laboratories can use the material from NIST in order to validate their tests and to determine test sensitivity, which is the lowest amount of genetic material that their tests can detect. Ultimately, the availability of this well-characterized NIST control material may serve to support more reliable and more rapidly implemented mpox testing across a range of laboratory settings.

The value of the NIST control material isn’t in the DNA itself, which is relatively easy to synthesize. Rather, it is NIST’s assurance that each vial of the material contains the same very precisely measured amount of DNA, to a known degree of certainty. To wit: Each microliter contains 110,000 copies of the DNA strand, plus or minus 10%.

NIST scientists analyzed the DNA to ensure there are no errors in the genetic sequences. They measured the concentration of DNA in the material using a high-precision technique called digital PCR. And they worked with NIST statisticians to ensure that each microliter of the material contains the same amount of DNA, within the stated bounds of uncertainty.

“We do a lot of work to make sure we get those numbers right,” said Scott Jackson, the NIST microbial geneticist who led the effort.

Commercial laboratories can use the material from NIST to validate their tests and to determine test sensitivity, which is the lowest amount of genetic material their tests can detect.

input:
The silicon optical cavity, which is compact enough to fit within an Artemis spacecraft, will be completely assembled on Earth, according to Wei Zhang, a co-author of the study from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory. During the deployment on the Moon, it will be necessary for the device’s radiation panels to unfold properly. Furthermore, astronauts will utilize a remote or mechanically controlled lunar rover to lower the cavity into the designated crater, as Zhang indicated.

It is worth noting that landing in the polar regions of the Moon may prove difficult due to inadequate illumination, as observed by co-author Yiqi Ni from Lunetronic. However, regions that are permanently shadowed on the Moon are considered essential for the long-term exploration of the lunar surface due to their potential to harbor water-ice and other vital resources required for sustaining a human presence.

Ultimately, Ni estimates that the demonstration of a silicon optical cavity in low-Earth orbit could occur within two years, with deployment on the lunar surface projected to take place within three to five years. The installation of the cavity inside a dark crater is anticipated to require coordinated efforts from multiple agencies. This information suggests a strategic approach to future lunar exploration initiatives.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/01/cells-electric-fields-keep-nanoparticles-bay-scientists-confirm
input: Additionally, Hoogerheide noted that the electric field near a membrane in a salty solution, such as those produced by the body, can often be astoundingly strong. Furthermore, its strength tends to experience a rapid decline with distance, which creates large field gradients that the team figured might repel nearby particles, and so they used neutron beams to look into it. Neutrons can distinguish between different isotopes of hydrogen, and the team designed experiments that explored a membrane’s effect on nearby molecules of PEG, a polymer that forms chargeless nano-sized particles. It is worth noting that hydrogen is a major constituent of PEG, and by immersing the membrane and PEG into a solution of heavy water, which is made with deuterium in place of ordinary water’s hydrogen atoms, the team could measure how closely the PEG particles approached the membrane. In essence, they used a technique known as neutron reflectometry at the NCNR as well as instruments at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Together with molecular dynamics simulations, the experiments revealed the first-ever evidence that the membranes’ powerful field gradients were the culprit behind the repulsion, in that the PEG molecules were more strongly repelled from charged surfaces than from neutral surfaces. While the findings do not reveal any fundamentally new physics, Hoogerheide said, they do show well-known physics in an unexpected place, and that should encourage scientists to take notice and explore it further. He added that the team needs to add this to its understanding of how things interact at the nanoscale, and that they have demonstrated the strength and significance of this interaction. Ultimately, he said, the team now needs to investigate how it affects these crowded environments where so much biology happens.

Neutrons can distinguish between different isotopes of hydrogen, and the team designed experiments that explored a membrane’s effect on nearby molecules of PEG, a polymer that forms chargeless nano-sized particles. Hydrogen is a major constituent of PEG, and by immersing the membrane and PEG into a solution of heavy water — which is made with deuterium in place of ordinary water’s hydrogen atoms — the team could measure how closely the PEG particles approached the membrane. They used a technique known as neutron reflectometry at the NCNR as well as instruments at Oak Ridge National Laboratory.

Together with molecular dynamics simulations, the experiments revealed the first-ever evidence that the membranes’ powerful field gradients were the culprit behind the repulsion: The PEG molecules were more strongly repelled from charged surfaces than from neutral surfaces.

While the findings do not reveal any fundamentally new physics, Hoogerheide said, they do show well-known physics in an unexpected place, and that should encourage scientists to take notice — and explore it further.

“We need to add this to our understanding of how things interact at the nanoscale,” he said. “We’ve demonstrated the strength and significance of this interaction. Now we need to investigate how it affects these crowded environments where so much biology happens.”

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/01/nist-database-can-help-increase-recycling-textiles-and-clothing
input:
At those centers, workers engage in the sorting of clothing by utilizing handheld devices that emit near-infrared light. These devices are capable of measuring the extent to which the light either passes through or scatters off the fabric, thereby generating a distinctive pattern that functions as a sort of fingerprint. This unique identifier can be instrumental in recognizing the types of fibers present in the clothing. This process, known as near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy, also finds application in automated conveyor belt systems; however, it is important to note that current techniques still necessitate substantial manual labor.

In recent years, manufacturers of recycling equipment have increasingly integrated machine learning and artificial intelligence into the enhancement of their sorting algorithms. In order to effectively train these algorithms, high-quality reference data is essential.

This is where the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) database becomes significant. This database, referred to as the Near-Infrared Spectra of Origin-defined and Real-world Textiles, or NIR-SORT, encompasses 64 distinct types of fabric along with the corresponding NIR fingerprints they yield. The database includes pure fiber types such as cotton and polyester, blended fiber types such as spandex blends, and real-world fabrics sourced from thrift stores. Manufacturers of NIR scanner systems can utilize this database to train and evaluate their sorting algorithms, thereby enhancing the performance of their products.

Notably, challenges arise when fibers exhibit similarities, such as cotton and hemp, leading to comparable near-infrared signals. The same issue applies to cotton and polyester blends, raising the question of whether a given sample is a new fiber or a blend of two or more fibers. Katarina Goodge, a NIST research chemist who spearheaded the development of the database, emphasizes that artificial intelligence has the potential to refine the decision-making process, thereby increasing accuracy.

Given that NIST serves as the nation’s measurement institute, it possesses both the equipment and the expertise necessary to populate this database with exceptionally high-quality spectral data. This advancement may lead to a reduction in errors associated with fabric identification, ultimately facilitating a greater volume of textiles being recycled. In summary, the integration of this sophisticated database and advanced technology appears to signify a promising step forward for the textile recycling industry.

input:
Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have developed a new device that may significantly enhance the process of converting heat into electricity. If this technology is further refined, it can potentially help recover some of the heat energy that is lost in the United States, which amounts to approximately $100 billion annually.

Notably, the innovative fabrication technique, which has been introduced by NIST researcher Kris Bertness along with her colleagues, involves the deposition of numerous microscopic columns made from gallium nitride on a silicon wafer. Subsequently, layers of silicon are removed from the bottom side of the wafer, leaving behind only a thin sheet of the material. The interaction between the columns and the silicon sheet tends to slow down the heat transfer within the silicon, thereby enabling a greater portion of the heat to be converted into electrical current. Bertness and her team from the University of Colorado Boulder shared their findings in the journal Advanced Materials on March 23.

Once this fabrication method reaches its full potential, it is conceivable that the silicon sheets could be applied around steam or exhaust pipes, allowing for the conversion of heat emissions into electricity that may be used to power nearby devices or integrated into a power grid. Furthermore, another possible application could involve the cooling of computer chips.

In essence, the study conducted by NIST and the University of Colorado is grounded in an intriguing phenomenon first identified by the German physicist Thomas Seebeck. During the early 1820s, Seebeck was investigating two metal wires, each composed of different materials, which were connected at both ends to form a loop. It is worth noting that when the two junctions of the wires were maintained at differing temperatures, a nearby compass needle exhibited a deflection. Subsequent researchers realized that this deflection occurred as a result of the temperature difference inducing a voltage between the two sections, leading to a flow of current from the hotter area to the cooler one. This current subsequently generated a magnetic field, which caused the compass needle to deflect. Ultimately, this historical discovery lays the foundation for the modern advancements being explored in heat-to-electricity conversion technology.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/07/out-shadows-new-imaging-method-reveals-concealed-objects
input:
Other methods that do not rely on a light source analyze the shadows created by hidden objects on surfaces or detect the heat, specifically infrared radiation, that is naturally emitted by concealed bodies and scattered into view. However, it is important to note that these techniques often demand substantial computing time and analysis. A good algorithm combined with significant computational power may extract images, yet the quality of these images may not be satisfactory, as mentioned by NIST physicist Erich Grossman.

Furthermore, Grossman and his team have developed a novel approach that focuses on detecting minimal quantities of longer wavelength radiation in the submillimeter range, which exists just beyond microwave radiation. This range, which encompasses wavelengths from 300 micrometers to 1 millimeter, tends to allow walls made from various materials to appear relatively smooth and function as partial mirrors, thereby reflecting rather than diffusely scattering the radiation emitted by hidden objects.

To create an image, it is necessary to direct and focus this reflected radiation. Unlike visible light, which can be manipulated using glass lenses, submillimeter radiation requires different methods for steering. Grossman and his colleagues utilized curved mirrors to concentrate the invisible light effectively.

In their experimental work with the prototype, Grossman and his collaborators at the University of Minnesota Twin Cities in Minneapolis demonstrated the capability to construct images of objects concealed behind walls within approximately 20 minutes. This innovative technique utilizes advanced indium phosphide transistors that amplify submillimeter radiation with minimal noise over a broad range of wavelengths, eliminating the need for complex algorithms or significant computer analysis. Grossman emphasized, "What is noteworthy about this method is its simplicity," as it does not involve quantum mechanics, relativity, or anything sophisticated, relying solely on transistors, a basic computer, and mirrors. Overall, the entire apparatus is compact enough to be carried in a backpack.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/05/shooting-moon-ultrastable-lasers-dark-craters-could-enable-lunar-navigation
input: Additionally, it is worth noting that these craters may possess an even higher vacuum than the lunar surface, which can often further reduce or eliminate vibrations arising from sound waves and stray particles that might strike the mirrors and alter the distance between them. Furthermore, by radiating any residual heat from the cavity system into the much colder abyss of outer space, the optical cavity could be cooled further, without the need for a cryostat or other equipment, to a temperature of 16 K. Moreover, at that temperature, silicon neither expands nor contracts when exposed to tiny changes in temperature, thereby ensuring that light entering the cavity always traverses exactly the same distance between the two mirrors. Once the optical silicon cavity is deployed, a commercially available laser would be placed nearby, either on the rim or inside the permanently shadowed crater. In essence, a small amount of laser light directed into the optical cavity would be used to lock the laser frequency to one of the resonant frequencies allowed by the cavity, ensuring that the laser emits light of a single unchanging color. After stabilizing the frequency of its light, the laser could act as a GPS-like signal, guiding lunar spacecraft to land safely, especially those set to touch down on dimly lit regions near the south pole. Additionally, by tuning its light to the signals of atomic clocks on satellites, a high-stability lunar laser could also form the backbone of the first optical atomic clock on an extraterrestrial surface. Ultimately, this timekeeping signal would rival those from the most precise and accurate optical atomic clocks on Earth, which Ye and colleagues have built in Earth-bound laboratories. In summary, the deployment of such a cavity system appears to offer a promising pathway toward unprecedented timekeeping and navigation capabilities on the lunar surface.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/06/nist-tree-nut-reference-materials-support-food-allergen-testing
input:
The researchers collaborated with a company to ensure the appropriate packaging of reference materials while minimizing the potential risks associated with cross-contact. Subsequently, they dispatched these materials to developers of test kits, who undertook their own testing of the reference materials. This involved comparing their findings with an analysis provided by the National Institute of Standards and Technology, or NIST. Additionally, they offered feedback regarding both their results and the testing methodologies they employed. This feedback mechanism proved beneficial by assisting NIST in validating its processes and confirming the quality of the final product.

Notably, RM 8404 Almond Flour for Allergen Detection and RM 8405 Hazelnut Flour for Allergen Detection are currently accessible at NIST. Organizations that are interested in acquiring these reference materials may visit the NIST Standard Reference Materials webpage. Ultimately, this collaboration and feedback process underscores the commitment to maintaining high standards in allergen detection.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2023/05/nist-team-demonstrates-novel-way-convert-heat-electricity
input:
The interaction that occurs between the phonons moving through the silicon sheet and the vibrations present in the nanopillars may lead to a reduction in the speed of these phonons, which can often hinder the transfer of heat through the material. Consequently, this phenomenon appears to diminish thermal conductivity, thereby increasing the temperature gradient from one end of the material to the other. Furthermore, it is noteworthy that the interaction among the phonons achieves this effect while leaving the electrical conductivity of the silicon sheet largely unaffected.

Additionally, the research team is currently engaged in the development of structures that are composed entirely of silicon, which may feature an improved geometry aimed at enhancing thermoelectric heat recovery. The researchers anticipate that their advancements may allow them to achieve a heat-to-electricity conversion rate that could potentially render their technique economically feasible for industrial applications.

This investigation has received partial funding from the Department of Energy’s Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy. It is worth noting that a recent update clarified that the $100 billion figure mentioned refers not to the total volume of waste heat produced, but rather to the portion of waste heat that can be recovered.

In summary, the research explores the manipulation of phonon interactions within silicon to improve thermal management, with promising implications for energy recovery technologies.

This reduces the thermal conductivity, thus increasing the temperature difference from one end to the other. Just as importantly, the phonon interaction accomplishes this feat while leaving the electrical conductivity of the silicon sheet unchanged.

The team is now working on structures fabricated entirely of silicon and with a better geometry for thermoelectric heat recovery. The researchers expect to demonstrate a heat-to-electricity conversion rate high enough to make their technique economically viable for industry.

Semiconductor thermal and electrical properties decoupled by localized phonon resonances. Advanced Materials. Published online March 23, 2023. DOI: 10.1002/adma.202209779

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/09/nist-funds-climate-measurements-center-excellence-university-vermont
input: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has reached an agreement with the University of Vermont (UVM) to establish a Climate Measurements Center of Excellence, and this cooperative arrangement includes an award of $2.7 million that was appropriated by Congress for the purpose. Furthermore, the agreement was reached following a competitive process that was announced earlier this year, and it appears to reflect a broader effort to strengthen the scientific foundation for climate adaptation. Notably, Chuck Romine, the associate director for laboratory programs at NIST, said that the goal is to advance trust in measurements and technology in service to the nation, and he noted that effective measurements are key to understanding the dynamics of complex climate systems. In essence, he suggested that this center of excellence can amplify the agency’s impact and enable the development of equitable climate adaptation plans. Additionally, climate impacts tend to be experienced differently from one region of the U.S. to another, and communities often need more granular information than is currently available in order to develop adaptation plans. Furthermore, the Climate Measurements Center of Excellence is intended to support communities through the provision of standards frameworks, regional data, and the tools that communities need for decision-making. It is worth noting that climate impacts at the community level are expected to be diverse, complex, and interrelated, and examples of possible impacts include diminished agricultural productivity, poor air quality, increased food costs, supply chain and commercial logistics disruptions, and public health issues. Ultimately, preparing for and mitigating these impacts can often be challenging for any one community alone, so the center will bring local climate researchers together for the sharing of resources and ideas. In addition, it will serve as a hub for stakeholders including government climate offices, universities, nonprofits, industry, and NIST, and this collaborative structure tends to support more coordinated responses. In summary, the new center appears designed to combine federal investment, regional data, and stakeholder collaboration in support of more informed community climate adaptation.

“Our goal is to advance trust in measurements and technology in service to the nation. Effective measurements are key to understanding the dynamics of complex climate systems, and this center of excellence can amplify our impact and enable the development of equitable climate adaptation plans,” said Chuck Romine, the associate director for laboratory programs at NIST.

Climate impacts are felt differently from one region of the U.S. to another, and for communities to develop adaptation plans, they need more granular information than is currently available. The Climate Measurements Center of Excellence will support communities by providing standards frameworks, regional data, and the tools communities need to make decisions.

Climate impacts at the community level are expected to be diverse, complex and interrelated. Examples of possible impacts include diminished agricultural productivity, poor air quality, increased food costs, supply chain and commercial logistics disruptions, and public health issues. Preparing for and mitigating these impacts could be challenging for any one community alone. Therefore, the center will bring local climate researchers together to share resources and ideas and will serve as a hub for stakeholders including government climate offices, universities, nonprofits, industry and NIST.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/08/nist-releases-first-3-finalized-post-quantum-encryption-standards
input:
The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), which operates under the U.S. Department of Commerce, has recently concluded the development of its primary set of encryption algorithms, which are intended to resist potential cyberattacks originating from quantum computers. 

Researchers globally are engaged in a competitive effort to create quantum computers that may function in fundamentally different manners compared to traditional computers. Such advancements could potentially compromise the effectiveness of current encryption methods that are crucial for ensuring security and privacy across various online activities. The encryption algorithms that NIST has announced today are detailed within the initial set of completed standards derived from NIST’s post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standardization project, and they are available for immediate application.

Furthermore, these three new standards are designed with a forward-looking perspective. The technology associated with quantum computing is advancing swiftly, and some experts estimate that a device capable of undermining existing encryption techniques could emerge within the next decade. This development poses significant risks to the security and privacy of individuals, organizations, and nations alike.

It is worth noting that the progression of quantum computing holds substantial implications for reaffirming America’s position as a leading technological entity while also influencing the future of economic security. Deputy Secretary of Commerce Don Graves emphasized this point by stating, “The advancement of quantum computing plays an essential role in reaffirming America’s status as a global technological powerhouse and driving the future of our economic security.” He further remarked that the various bureaus within the Department of Commerce are committed to ensuring U.S. competitiveness in the quantum domain, particularly through the efforts of NIST, which is taking a proactive stance in this comprehensive governmental initiative. 

NIST is contributing critical expertise toward the development of innovative approaches to quantum-related challenges, including security strategies such as post-quantum cryptography that organizations can begin to adopt for safeguarding their future in a post-quantum landscape. As this extensive endeavor progresses over the next decade, there is optimism about advancing the legacy of leadership that the Department of Commerce has established in this essential area.
human:
The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has finalized its principal set of encryption algorithms designed to withstand cyberattacks from a quantum computer.

Researchers around the world are racing to build quantum computers that would operate in radically different ways from ordinary computers and could break the current encryption that provides security and privacy for just about everything we do online. The algorithms announced today are specified in the first completed standards from NIST’s post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standardization project, and are ready for immediate use.

The three new standards are built for the future. title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/07/nist-develops-genetic-material-validating-mpox-tests
input:
The material produced by the National Institute of Standards and Technology, or NIST, can also be utilized in the monitoring of wastewater for the presence of a virus, which may indicate whether a virus exists within a community and the extent of its prevalence. Furthermore, this specific type of monitoring can often be complicated by the significant dilution of the virus in wastewater, while researchers may employ the control to verify the accuracy of their testing processes.

In the year 2020, NIST made available a comparable positive control material intended for SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. That specific material was instrumental in assisting with the standardization of tests designed for the disease.

NIST is known for producing thousands of standard reference materials, commonly referred to as SRMs, which are essential for ensuring precise measurements across a variety of industries. The agency is now releasing this positive control as a "research grade test material," as it has not yet completed the comprehensive series of evaluations necessary for classification as a NIST SRM. For instance, researchers are still investigating how the attributes of the material may change over time.

NIST is offering this material at no cost to any test manufacturer or testing laboratory globally, thus promoting widespread access. Additionally, technical information and detailed instructions for obtaining the material can be found on the NIST website.

This page received an update on December 6, 2022, reflecting the decision made by the World Health Organization to rename the virus previously known as “monkeypox” to “mpox.” Ultimately, these developments highlight NIST's commitment to advancing public health monitoring and testing standards.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/07/nanomagnets-can-choose-wine-and-could-slake-ais-thirst-energy
input:
Human brains are capable of processing substantial amounts of information. When wine enthusiasts evaluate a new wine, neural networks within their brains engage in the processing of various data points derived from each sip. Furthermore, synapses within their neurons become activated, assessing the significance of each data element—such as acidity, fruitiness, and bitterness—before transmitting this information to subsequent layers of neurons in the network. As this information progresses, the brain is able to distinguish the specific type of wine being tasted.

Notably, scientists aspire for artificial intelligence (AI) systems to achieve comparable levels of sophistication in data processing, which has led to the creation of computer-based models of neural networks designed for information analysis. Although AI is advancing toward human capabilities in numerous tasks, it typically requires significantly greater energy to perform similar functions. In comparison, human brains are estimated to operate using an average of 20 watts of power, while an AI system can consume energy levels thousands of times greater. Additionally, this hardware can experience delays, resulting in AI being slower, less efficient, and less effective than human cognitive processes. Consequently, a significant area of AI research is focused on identifying alternatives that are less energy-intensive.

In a recent study published in the journal Physical Review Applied, scientists from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), along with their collaborators, have introduced a novel type of hardware for AI. This innovation has the potential to utilize less energy and improve operational speed, as evidenced by its successful performance in a virtual wine-tasting assessment. Ultimately, these advancements may lead to more efficient AI systems that better emulate human cognitive capabilities.

As information flows, the brain parses out the type of wine.

Scientists want artificial intelligence (AI) systems to be sophisticated data connoisseurs too, and so they design computer versions of neural networks to process and analyze information. AI is catching up to the human brain in many tasks, but usually consumes a lot more energy to do the same things. Our brains make these calculations while consuming an estimated average of 20 watts of power. An AI system can use thousands of times that. Now, in a study published in the journal Physical Review Applied, scientists at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and their collaborators have developed a new type of hardware for AI that could use less energy and operate more quickly — and it has already passed a virtual wine-tasting test.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2025/08/nist-provide-updates-construction-safety-team-investigations-september
input:
GAITHERSBURG, Maryland — The United States Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is scheduled to host two virtual meetings for the National Construction Safety Team Advisory Committee on September 9 and September 16, 2025. These public meetings will serve to provide updates regarding NIST’s ongoing investigations into the consequences of Hurricane Maria, which occurred in 2017 and affected Puerto Rico, as well as the partial collapse of the Champlain Towers South building in Surfside, Florida, in 2021.

In addition to the presentations focusing on these current investigations, the meetings will incorporate updates concerning the progress achieved in implementing recommendations from prior investigations and the responses to the committee’s recommendations for the year 2024.

The presentations and discussions pertaining to Hurricane Maria and the Champlain Towers South incident are scheduled to occur on Tuesday, September 9. Furthermore, the meeting on September 16 will include updates regarding NIST’s Disaster and Failure Studies Program. A detailed agenda will be made available on the NCST Advisory Committee Meetings webpage once it has been finalized.

Individuals who are interested in attending the virtual meetings can complete their registration on the NIST event page. The link to access the meetings will be distributed to those who have registered shortly before September 9.

It is important to note that the meeting on September 9 will feature a period dedicated to public comments. Individuals wishing to provide comments must ensure they register by 5:00 p.m. EDT on Thursday, September 4, 2025, via the aforementioned link, and clearly indicate their desire to deliver a comment.

In July 2025, the lead investigator for the Hurricane Maria investigation, Joe Main, along with co-lead Maria Dillard, released a video update that included preliminary findings and potential recommendations related to their research. Additional information regarding this investigation is accessible on the NIST website.

Moreover, Judith Mitrani-Reiser, who leads the Champlain Towers South investigation, along with co-lead Glenn Bell, provided a technical video update regarding their investigation in June 2025. All publicly available information concerning this investigation, which includes videos, photographs, and presentation slides, can be found on the NIST website.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/07/out-shadows-new-imaging-method-reveals-concealed-objects
input:
A novel technique for imaging concealed objects, developed by a researcher at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) together with his colleagues, may well diminish the enjoyment associated with games such as hide-and-seek, yet it also appears to offer significant potential for saving lives. The capacity to image scenes located beyond an observer's direct line of sight can often greatly enhance search and rescue missions, for example the location of a lost child within an abandoned factory, and it may likewise strengthen military and police surveillance operations, such as the exposure of a hidden terrorist or an enemy stronghold. Furthermore, the ability to see around corners and to reconstruct a complete image of a concealed object or obstacle in real time could someday contribute to improvements in robotic vision as well as in the safety and accuracy of self-driving cars, although it is worth noting that the prototype method cannot presently generate an image instantaneously.

Most conventional approaches to imaging objects behind an obstruction tend to rely on an external light source, such as ultra-short pulses of visible or infrared laser light. In essence, the light source initially illuminates a wall that scatters the light into the concealed region, and when the light subsequently strikes a hidden object, the object re-scatters a portion of that light back to the wall, where detection can then occur.

However, the imaging of hidden objects through the use of visible and infrared light alone is often challenging. At those relatively short wavelengths, a typical wall, regardless of how smooth it may appear to the human touch, presents itself as a rough surface and consequently scatters incoming light in all directions. As a result, it reveals less information about objects than light reflected from a smooth or mirrored surface would provide, and it requires sophisticated algorithms together with significant computing time to produce even a semi-sharp image. Additionally, the illumination may tip off adversaries that they are under surveillance. Ultimately, the proposed method appears to offer notable advantages over conventional approaches, even though further development is likely required before its full potential can be realized.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2022/02/commerce-department-awards-54-million-american-rescue-act-grants-increase
input:
MxD, located in Chicago, Illinois, received a funding allocation of $3,880,343 aimed at the development of the Rx Product Marketplace Orchestrator, which serves as an online platform for both consumers and manufacturers of emergency health and medical supplies. This initiative strives to ensure a rapid response throughout the supply chain to effectively meet the demand for specific items such as respirators, ventilators, and face masks, and it involves collaboration with nine partner organizations.

Furthermore, the RAPID Institute, associated with the American Institute of Chemical Engineers in New York, New York, was awarded $3,773,536 to enhance continuous manufacturing and modular production techniques. The focus of this funding is to produce high-quality and low-cost advanced respirators and biosensors, which may serve to limit exposure to and transmission of coronavirus. This effort includes collaboration with four partner organizations.

Additionally, America Makes, the National Center for Defense Manufacturing and Machining based in Youngstown, Ohio, received $3,021,989 to utilize additive manufacturing for the creation of a prototype of N95-level nonwoven filter materials intended for respiratory personal protective equipment (PPE). This initiative is designed to meet the requirements set forth by the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration while simultaneously reducing reliance on foreign imports. The project also involves a partnership with a local community college and small to medium-sized manufacturers aimed at training workers in advanced manufacturing applications, incorporating six partner organizations in this effort.

Moreover, MxD in Chicago, Illinois, has been allocated $2,369,302 to develop a local health alert system that protects privacy while conducting contact tracing and data analysis through blockchain technology. This system is designed to map the relationships between disease detection and the resulting supply chain demand estimates, thereby transforming real-time public health indicators into predictive capabilities for future supply chain needs. This initiative is supported by the collaboration of seven partner organizations.

Finally, the RAPID Institute in New York, New York, has received $1,109,520 to create and implement virtual training programs specifically for technicians and operators involved in advanced processes within the biopharmaceutical, pharmaceutical, and specialty chemical industries. This initiative is being executed in partnership with three partner organizations. In summary, these initiatives collectively aim to enhance the production and distribution of critical health and medical goods while advancing manufacturing training and capabilities.

The goal is to make sure the supply chain can respond quickly to meet needs like respirators, ventilators, and face masks. It works with nine partner groups.

The RAPID Institute, part of the American Institute of Chemical Engineers in New York, got $3.7 million to improve continuous manufacturing and modular production. The money is for making high-quality, low-cost respirators and biosensors that can help stop coronavirus spread. It works with four partner groups.

America Makes, based in Youngstown, Ohio, got $3.0 million to use 3D printing to make a prototype of N95-level nonwoven filters for PPE. The project follows guidelines from the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health and the FDA. It also trains workers at a community college and small manufacturers. It works with six partner groups.

MxD in Chicago also got $2.3 million to build a local health alert system using blockchain. It tracks disease detection and supply chain needs, turning real-time health data into predictions. It works with seven partner groups.

The RAPID Institute in New York got $1.1 million to create virtual training for technicians and operators in biopharma, pharma, and specialty chemicals. It works with three partner groups.

All these projects aim to boost production and distribution of critical health goods and improve manufacturing training.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/05/shooting-moon-ultrastable-lasers-dark-craters-could-enable-lunar-navigation
input:
Additionally, these craters are considered to be among the darkest and coldest locations within the solar system. It is worth noting that hundreds of lunar craters, with many situated at the Moon's south pole, never experience direct sunlight and remain in a state of permanent shadow. Consequently, physicist Jun Ye and his colleagues have proposed that these craters may serve as an ideal location for the construction of a critical component for an ultrastable laser.

Furthermore, a highly stable laser on the Moon, which can be described as a source of coherent light that maintains a nearly constant frequency or color, could potentially provide a master time signal. In addition, such a laser appears to offer GPS-like navigation capabilities for lunar operations, according to Ye, who maintains affiliations with both the National Institute of Standards and Technology and JILA. It is worth noting that JILA itself is a joint institute of NIST and the University of Colorado Boulder. Ultimately, multiple copies of these lunar lasers could be utilized to measure distances between objects with precision and may potentially detect exotic physics phenomena, such as ripples in space-time.

Additionally, the construction of a lunar laser would require astronauts to first install a key component that is known as an optical silicon cavity. In essence, this device consists of a block of silicon that permits only certain frequencies of light to bounce back and forth between mirrors located on each end of the block. Notably, the distance between the two mirrors tends to determine the frequencies that are allowed to resonate within the cavity. Furthermore, for a highly stable optical cavity, that distance, and therefore those frequencies, does not appear to vary over time.

Furthermore, the Moon can often be regarded as an ideal location for the construction of an optical cavity because it is subject to relatively few vibrations when compared with Earth. Additionally, the lunar environment tends to possess a high vacuum, since it is devoid of air. In essence, these conditions may contribute to the overall stability and performance of such a device.

Additionally, the permanently shadowed craters located at the lunar south pole appear to provide an even greater advantage for this purpose. It is worth noting that their frigid temperature of approximately 50 kelvins, or 50 degrees above absolute zero, can drastically reduce the random jitter of the mirrored surfaces. Ultimately, these combined environmental factors may make such locations highly suitable for the construction of an ultrastable laser component.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2023/07/new-nist-measurements-aim-advance-and-validate-portable-mri-technology
input:
Additionally, the researchers gathered images of the entire brain and obtained data on its gray matter, which contains a high concentration of nerve cells, along with white matter and cerebrospinal fluid. It is worth noting that white matter refers to the deeper tissues of the brain that house nerve fibers, while cerebrospinal fluid is the clear fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord. Furthermore, these three brain constituents tend to respond to the low magnetic field in different ways and produce distinctive signals that reflect their unique properties. Consequently, the MRI system can produce images that contain quantitative information about each constituent, which appears to be a significant advantage. "Knowing the quantitative properties of tissue allows us to develop new image collection strategies for this MRI system," said NIST biomedical engineer Katy Keenan.

In essence, MRI contrast agents are magnetic materials that are injected into patients and enhance image contrast, and they make it easier for radiologists to identify anatomical features or evidence of disease. Additionally, these agents are routinely used in MRI at conventional magnetic field strengths, but researchers are just starting to understand how they might be used with the new low-field MRI scanners. At the lower field strengths of these scanners, contrast agents may act differently than at higher field strengths, which can often create opportunities to use new types of magnetic materials for image enhancement.

Furthermore, NIST scientists and their colleagues compared the sensitivity of several magnetic contrast agents in low magnetic fields. Notably, the researchers found that iron oxide nanoparticles outperformed traditional contrast agents, which are made of the element gadolinium, a rare-earth metal. At low magnetic field strength, the nanoparticles provided good contrast using a concentration of only about one-ninth that of the gadolinium particles. Ultimately, these findings suggest that iron oxide nanoparticles may serve as an effective alternative for low-field MRI applications.

title: https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/03/nist-physicist-sae-woo-nam-pioneer-single-photon-detectors-passes-away
input:
In essence, Sae Woo was recognized as a creative force in the scientific community, characterized by both a robust scientific acumen and a strong ethical framework. His humility and determination led him to embrace any role necessary to further the advancement of science. 

Throughout the duration of his scientific career, Sae Woo received a multitude of prestigious awards and honors. Notably, he was bestowed the Gold Medal in 2011, which represents the highest accolade from the Department of Commerce. Additionally, in 2008, he received the NIST Jacob Rabinow Applied Research Award in recognition of his groundbreaking efficient photon detectors. Furthermore, he was honored with the Arthur S. Flemming Award for contributions to Applied Science, Engineering, and Mathematics. In 2017, he achieved the distinction of earning the Presidential Rank Award for his significant advancements in quantum information. Moreover, in 2020, he attained the status of APS Fellow, while also being named an Optica Fellow in 2011 and an IEEE Fellow in 2022. It is worth noting that the contributions of Sae Woo and his colleagues in the examination of Bell’s Inequality Theorem were cited in the 2022 Nobel Prize for Physics.

His wife and colleague, NIST chemist Kimberly Briggman, remarked, “In addition to his brilliance, Sae Woo was both fearless and humble. He was passionate about improving both the world around him and NIST. He valued the principles of diversity and inclusion and challenged the people around him to do their absolute best. Perhaps a little-known fact about Sae Woo is that despite all of his accomplishments and awards, he was always embarrassed to take credit. Instead, he attributed any successes of his programs to his team of colleagues and coworkers.”

Additionally, outside of his dedication to science, Sae Woo engaged in various athletic pursuits, including rock climbing, mountain biking, ice hockey, and snowboarding. Furthermore, he demonstrated a passion for culinary exploration, frequently gathering friends and coworkers to experiment with new recipes and share meals together. In summary, Sae Woo exemplified a multifaceted individual whose contributions to science and community were profound and lasting.

title: A Modest Proposal
input:
To prevent the children of impoverished families in Ireland from becoming a burden on their parents or society, and to ensure they contribute positively to the public good, attention must be directed toward their situation. 

It is a sorrowful sight for those who walk through the city or travel in the countryside. They observe the streets, roads, and doorways crowded with female beggars accompanied by three, four, or even six ragged children. These mothers are unable to earn a legitimate income and must dedicate all their time to begging for food to support their vulnerable infants. As these children grow, they often resort to theft due to a lack of employment opportunities, leave their homeland to fight for the Pretender in Spain, or sell themselves into servitude in the Caribbean.

These mothers, instead of being able to work for their honest livelihood, are forced to employ all their time in stroling to beg sustenance for their helpless infants who, as they grow up, either turn thieves for want of work, or leave their dear native country, to fight for the Pretender in Spain, or sell themselves to the Barbadoes.

title: A Modest Proposal
input:
I am assured by our merchants that a child, whether male or female, under the age of twelve years is not a marketable commodity. Furthermore, even upon reaching this age, such individuals will not fetch more than three pounds, or at most three pounds and half a crown in the marketplace. This situation proves disadvantageous for both the parents and the kingdom, as the expenses of sustenance and clothing have amounted to at least four times that value. 

In essence, I shall now humbly present my own thoughts on the matter, which I trust will not encounter any objections.

title: A Modest Proposal
input: It is widely acknowledged by all involved that the considerable number of children being carried in the arms, on the backs, or trailing behind their mothers, and often their fathers, represents a significant additional grievance within the current lamentable state of the kingdom. Furthermore, anyone who could devise a just, economical, and straightforward approach to transforming these children into healthy and valuable members of the commonwealth would merit exceptional recognition from the public, potentially warranting the erection of a statue in their honor as a preserver of the nation.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
input:
They approached the Mock Turtle, who regarded them with tearful eyes but remained silent. 

They took a seat, and for several moments, no one spoke. Alice contemplated the situation, thinking it unlikely for him to conclude without starting. Nevertheless, she chose to remain patient.

This led to a prolonged silence, interrupted occasionally by the Gryphon's outbursts of "Hjckrrh!" and the Mock Turtle's continuous weeping. Alice almost stood up to express her gratitude for what she perceived as an interesting story, yet she held back, sensing that there might be more to hear, so she remained quiet.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
input:
An enormous puppy gazed down at her with large, round eyes, and feebly extended one paw, attempting to make contact with her. "Poor little creature!" remarked Alice in a coaxing tone, as she earnestly attempted to whistle to it; however, she was persistently terrified at the thought that it might be hungry, which could result in its consuming her despite her efforts at coaxing.

Barely aware of her actions, she picked up a small stick and offered it to the puppy. Consequently, the puppy leaped into the air, propelling itself off all four feet simultaneously with a delighted yelp, and rushed towards the stick, feigning an intent to worry it. In response, Alice sought refuge behind a large thistle to avoid being overwhelmed. The moment she reappeared on the opposite side, the puppy made another dash for the stick, tumbling head over heels in its eagerness to seize it. Alice, perceiving the situation as reminiscent of engaging in play with a cart-horse and anticipating the imminent possibility of being trampled, circled back around the thistle. Subsequently, the puppy initiated a series of brief charges toward the stick, moving only a short distance forward each time while retreating a considerable distance back, all the while barking hoarsely. Eventually, it settled down at a distance, panting, with its tongue lolling out of its mouth and its large eyes partially closed.

Hardly knowing what she did, she picked up a little bit of stick, and held it out to the puppy; whereupon the puppy jumped into the air off all its feet at once, with a yelp of delight, and rushed at the stick, and made believe to worry it; then Alice dodged behind a great thistle, to keep herself from being run over; and the moment she appeared on the other side, the puppy made another rush at the stick, and tumbled head over heels in its hurry to get hold of it; then Alice, thinking it was very like having a game of play with a cart-horse, and expecting every moment to be trampled under its feet, ran round the thistle again; then the puppy began a series of short charges at the stick, running a very little way forwards each time and a long way back, and barking hoarsely all the while, till at last it sat down a good way off, panting, with its tongue hanging out of its mouth, and its great eyes half shut.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
input: Alice encountered some challenges at the beginning, particularly with her flamingo. She managed to secure its body comfortably under her arm, allowing its legs to dangle down, but typically, just as she had the neck positioned straight, and was ready to strike the hedgehog, the flamingo would twist around to gaze up at her with a confused expression. This often made her laugh. When she finally got its head back down and prepared to try again, it could be quite frustrating to find that the hedgehog had rolled itself up and was attempting to crawl away. Additionally, there were often obstacles in the form of ridges or furrows that got in the way of where she wanted to direct the hedgehog. Given that the soldiers nearby were frequently standing up and moving to different spots, Alice soon realized that this game was quite challenging. Overall, her experience illustrated how complicated the situation could be.

title: The Secret Garden
input: Mary received her meals consistently, with Martha serving her, but there was a noticeable lack of concern for her well-being. Mrs. Medlock visited every few days to check on her, yet no one engaged with her about her activities or provided guidance on what she should do. This situation led Mary to believe that it might be typical in England to treat children this way. In India, she had always been attended to by her Ayah, who was constantly by her side and catered to her needs. While she sometimes found her presence tiresome, the contrast to her current situation was stark. Now, she was alone and beginning to learn how to dress herself, as Martha often looked at her with a sense of disapproval when she requested assistance.

title: Treasure Island
input: I opened my eyes immediately. All around me were small ripples, moving over with a sharp, bristling sound and a slight phosphorescence. The HISPANIOLA herself, a few yards in whose wake I was still being carried along, appeared to stagger in her course, and I observed her spars toss a little against the darkness of the night; indeed, as I looked longer, I became certain that she was also turning toward the south. I glanced over my shoulder, and my heart leaped against my ribs. There, directly behind me, was the glow of the camp-fire. The current had turned at right angles, sweeping along with it the tall schooner and the small dancing coracle; ever accelerating, ever rising higher, ever murmuring more loudly, it went spinning through the narrows toward the open sea.

title: Treasure Island
input: Of the eight men who had fallen during the battle, only three remained alive: one pirate who had been shot at the loophole, Hunter, and Captain Smollett. However, the first two were effectively beyond saving. The mutineer succumbed to his injuries under the doctor's care, while Hunter, despite our best efforts, never regained consciousness. He struggled throughout the day, breathing heavily like an old buccaneer suffering from an apoplectic fit. Unfortunately, his chest had been crushed by the impact, and his skull was fractured from the fall. Sometime during the following night, without any sign or sound, he passed away.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: The eyes of moles and certain burrowing rodents are rudimentary in size, and in some cases they are entirely covered by skin and fur. This condition of the eyes is probably the result of gradual reduction through disuse, although it may also have been aided by natural selection. In South America, a burrowing rodent known as the tuco-tuco, or Ctenomys, is even more subterranean in its habits than the mole. A Spaniard who had often caught these animals assured me that they were frequently blind. One that I kept alive was certainly in this condition, and dissection showed that the cause was inflammation of the nictitating membrane. Since frequent inflammation of the eyes must be harmful to any animal, and since eyes are certainly not indispensable to animals with subterranean habits, a reduction in their size, together with the adhesion of the eyelids and the growth of fur over them, might in such a case be an advantage. If this were so, natural selection would constantly aid the effects of disuse.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: In the case of animals with separate sexes, the capacity to prevent crosses constitutes an important element of success in the formation of new races, at least in a country that is already stocked with other races. Additionally, in this respect the enclosure of the land plays a part. Moreover, wandering savages or the inhabitants of open plains rarely possess more than one breed of the same species. Furthermore, pigeons can be mated for life, and this is a great convenience to the fancier, for in this manner many races may be kept true, though mingled in the same aviary, and this circumstance must have largely favoured the improvement and formation of new breeds. It is worth noting that pigeons, I may add, can be propagated in great numbers and at a very quick rate, and inferior birds may be freely rejected, since when killed they serve for food. In essence, on the other hand, cats, from their nocturnal rambling habits, cannot be matched, and, although so much valued by women and children, we hardly ever see a distinct breed kept up; such breeds as we do sometimes see are almost always imported from some other country, often from islands. Additionally, although I do not doubt that some domestic animals vary less than others, yet the rarity or absence of distinct breeds of the cat, the donkey, peacock, goose, and so forth, may be attributed in main part to selection not having been brought into play: in cats, from the difficulty in pairing them; in donkeys, from only a few being kept by poor people, and little attention paid to their breeding; in peacocks, from not being very easily reared and a large stock not kept; in geese, from being valuable only for two purposes, food and feathers, and more especially from no pleasure having been felt in the display of distinct breeds.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: This highlights the observation that we know nothing about the origin or history of any of our domestic breeds. In reality, a breed, much like a dialect of a language, can hardly be said to have had a definite origin. A man preserves and breeds from an individual with some slight deviation of structure, or takes more care than usual in matching his best animals, thereby improving them, and the improved individuals slowly spread in the immediate neighbourhood. At this stage, however, they will hardly have a distinct name, and since they are only slightly valued, their history will be disregarded. When further improved through the same slow and gradual process, they will spread more widely and come to be recognised as something distinct and valuable, and will then probably first receive a provincial name. In semi-civilised countries with little free communication, the spreading and knowledge of any new sub-breed will be a slow process. Once the points of value of the new sub-breed are fully acknowledged, the principle of unconscious selection will always tend to slowly add to the characteristic features of the breed, whatever they may be, perhaps more at one period than another as the breed rises or falls in fashion, and perhaps more in one district than another according to the state of civilisation of the inhabitants. Ultimately, the chance of any record having been preserved of such slow, varying, and insensible changes will be infinitely small.

But the chance will be infinitely small of any record having been preserved of such slow, varying, and insensible changes.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: It is important to note that the process may not occur as consistently as illustrated in the diagram, even if it is somewhat irregular. It is not necessarily the case that the most distinct varieties will always dominate and reproduce; a more moderate form may often persist for extended periods and might or might not lead to more than one altered descendant. Natural selection typically operates based on the specific characteristics of environments that are either unoccupied or not fully occupied by other organisms, which can be influenced by a multitude of complex interactions. Generally speaking, the more varied in structure the descendants from a single species can become, the better their chances of exploiting different niches, which may lead to an increase in their modified offspring. In the diagram, the line of succession appears to be interrupted at regular intervals, indicated by small numbered letters that represent the distinct forms recognized as varieties. However, these interruptions are theoretical and could have been placed at various points, assuming sufficient time for significant divergent variation to accumulate. Overall, the complexity of these processes highlights the nuanced nature of evolutionary change.
human: But I must here remark that I do not suppose that the process ever goes on so regularly as is represented in the diagram, though in itself made somewhat irregular. I am far from thinking that the most divergent varieties will invariably prevail and multiply: a medium form may often long endure, and may or may not produce more than one modified descendant; for natural selection will always act according to the nature of the places which are either unoccupied or not perfectly occupied by other beings; and this will depend on infinitely complex relations. But as a general rule, the more diversified in structure the descendants from any one species can be rendered, the more places they will be enabled to seize on, and the more their modified progeny will be increased. In our diagram the line of succession is broken at regular intervals by small numbered letters marking the successive forms which have become sufficiently distinct to be recorded as varieties. But these breaks are imaginary, and might have been inserted anywhere, after intervals long enough to have allowed the accumulation of a considerable amount of divergent variation.
base: The diagram shows a process that may not happen as regularly as it appears. Some forms might not always be the most distinct; a less extreme one could stay around for a long time and maybe produce several different versions. Natural selection depends on the specific traits of places that aren’t fully filled by other life, and that’s shaped by many different factors. The more different a species’ descendants can be, the better they can fit into different roles, which might make their changes more likely. In the diagram, the line of change stops at regular spots, marked by small letters for the different forms. But these breaks are just ideas—they could have happened anywhere if there was enough time for big changes to happen. All in all, these processes show how complicated and careful evolution really is.
finetuned: But, in reality, the process of succession is not so regular as represented in the diagram, although it is somewhat irregular. It is not that the most distinct varieties will always succeed each other and reproduce; but a more moderate form may often exist for a long period, and may or may not produce more than one modified descendant. Natural selection acts on the particular characters of an unoccupied or partially occupied environment, and these are affected by a thousand complex relations. The more varied in structure the descendants from one species are, the better their chance of occupying different niches, and the more likely they are to produce modified descendants. In the diagram the line of succession is interrupted at regular intervals by the small lettered numbers representing the distinct forms known as varieties; but these interruptions are imaginary, and might have been placed at any points, provided sufficient time had elapsed for considerable divergent variation to have been accumulated.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: This passage summarizes the conditions that can influence natural selection, focusing on both favorable and unfavorable factors. It suggests that a large continental area, which is likely to experience significant fluctuations in elevation, is conducive to the emergence of diverse life forms that may thrive and expand over time. Initially, when this area exists as a continent, its diverse population will face intense competition. As subsidence transforms the continent into separate islands, many individuals of the same species will remain on each island, leading to restricted interbreeding at the edges of their ranges. This isolation, coupled with any physical changes, will hinder immigration, necessitating that new ecological niches be filled by adaptations of existing species. Over time, these modifications can lead to well-defined varieties. Should the islands eventually be uplifted back into a continental form, competition will resurge, allowing the more advantageous varieties to proliferate. This process may result in the extinction of less adapted forms, altering the relative proportions of the continent's inhabitants and providing further opportunities for natural selection to drive the evolution of new species.
human: To sum up the circumstances favourable and unfavourable to natural selection, as far as the extreme intricacy of the subject permits. I conclude, looking to the future, that for terrestrial productions a large continental area, which will probably undergo many oscillations of level, and which consequently will exist for long periods in a broken condition, will be the most favourable for the production of many new forms of life, likely to endure long and to spread widely. For the area will first have existed as a continent, and the inhabitants, at this period numerous in individuals and kinds, will have been subjected to very severe competition. When converted by subsidence into large separate islands, there will still exist many individuals of the same species on each island: intercrossing on the confines of the range of each species will thus be checked: after physical changes of any kind, immigration will be prevented, so that new places in the polity of each island will have to be filled up by modifications of the old inhabitants; and time will be allowed for the varieties in each to become well modified and perfected. When, by renewed elevation, the islands shall be re-converted into a continental area, there will again be severe competition: the most favoured or improved varieties will be enabled to spread: there will be much extinction of the less improved forms, and the relative proportional numbers of the various inhabitants of the renewed continent will again be changed; and again there will be a fair field for natural selection to improve still further the inhabitants, and thus produce new species.
base: This passage talks about what can affect natural selection, both good and bad things. A big land area that changes a lot in height is good for many different life forms to come up. When this area is a continent, the different animals and plants there have to compete a lot. But when the land goes down and becomes islands, the same species end up on each island. That means they can’t mix much, so they have to adapt to their own environment. If the islands go back up into one big land, the competition comes back, and the best adapted ones survive. Over time, this can lead to new species. Some of the old ones might go extinct, changing the mix of life and giving more chances for new evolution to happen.
finetuned: We may here briefly state the conditions under which natural selection will be most effective, and the agents which will most strongly influence it. The most powerful agent is the presence of a large continental area, which is, as I have shown, likely to be subject to great variations in elevation, and thus to produce the most diversified forms of life, which are most likely to thrive and multiply. When this large area is yet a continent, the whole population will be in the greatest degree subjected to fierce competition. When, however, subsidence has divided the continent into a number of islands, all the individuals of the same species will be on each island, and will be limited in their range, and thus restricted from interbreeding at the edges of their range. This isolation, together with any physical changes, will prevent immigration, and thus will force the new and modified form to occupy the new and unfilled ecological niche, and to be thus modified by the action of natural selection. In this way the new and modified form may become well marked and well defined. If the islands should be afterwards raised into a continental form, competition will again be fierce, and the more improved forms will increase in numbers, and the less improved will be exterminated. The relative proportions of the inhabitants of the continent will thus be changed, and the same process will be repeated, and natural selection will again be active.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: Natural selection may be a powerful process when compared to human selection, influencing traits that might seem trivial in importance. It appears to operate across various ages and can affect both males and females. Sexual selection also plays a role in this process. There tends to be a general tendency for interbreeding among individuals of the same species, which can be influenced by both favorable and unfavorable conditions for natural selection, including factors such as intercrossing, isolation, and population size. The effects of natural selection may often be slow and gradual, and it can lead to extinction in certain cases. The divergence of characteristics seems to be linked to the variety of organisms in small areas and the process of naturalization. Overall, the actions of natural selection through the divergence of traits and extinction contribute to the evolution of descendants from a shared ancestor, providing an explanation for the categorization of all living organisms.
human: Natural Selection: its power compared with man’s selection, its power on characters of trifling importance, its power at all ages and on both sexes. Sexual Selection. On the generality of intercrosses between individuals of the same species. Circumstances favourable and unfavourable to Natural Selection, namely, intercrossing, isolation, number of individuals. Slow action. Extinction caused by Natural Selection. Divergence of Character, related to the diversity of inhabitants of any small area, and to naturalisation. Action of Natural Selection, through Divergence of Character and Extinction, on the descendants from a common parent. Explains the Grouping of all organic beings.
base: Natural selection is a strong force when compared to human choice. It shapes traits that might seem unimportant. It works over many years and affects both men and women. Sexual selection is part of this too. Animals often mate with others of their kind, and this can be shaped by good or bad conditions. Factors like mixing with others, being separated, and how many there are all matter. Natural selection can be slow, and in some cases, it leads to extinction. Differences between species seem to come from many organisms in small areas and from when new species settle in new places. Overall, natural selection through these changes and extinctions helps explain how life forms have evolved from a common ancestor, which is why all living things are grouped together.
finetuned: Natural selection, as compared with man's choice, is a powerful agent in the production of differences which in the first instance are of trifling importance, and acts on all ages, on both sexes, and, as we have seen, on the sex of the young. Sexual selection is also an agent. There is a general tendency to interbreeding between individuals of the same species, which, as we have seen, is subject to the action of both the causes which are favorable and the causes which are unfavorable to natural selection, viz., intercrossing, isolation, and number of individuals. The effects of natural selection are generally slow and gradual, and may sometimes be fatal to the species. The divergence of characters is the result of the variety of beings in small areas and of the process of naturalization.

title: On the Origin of Species
input: If species are considered to be distinct and stable varieties, it may be easier to understand why their hybrid offspring might exhibit similar complex patterns in terms of resemblance to their parents. This includes being blended through successive crossings and other related characteristics, much like the hybrid offspring of recognized varieties. Conversely, these observations could appear puzzling if species were created independently while varieties were formed through secondary processes. Ultimately, this raises important questions about the nature of species and varieties in the context of their relationships and origins.
human: If species be only well-marked and permanent varieties, we can at once see why their crossed offspring should follow the same complex laws in their degrees and kinds of resemblance to their parents, - in being absorbed into each other by successive crosses, and in other such points, - as do the crossed offspring of acknowledged varieties. On the other hand, these would be strange facts if species have been independently created, and varieties have been produced by secondary laws.
base: If species are seen as distinct and stable, it's easier to explain why their hybrids might show similar complex patterns like their parents. They can blend over many crossings and share other traits, just like hybrids between known varieties. But if species were created separately and varieties came from later changes, these observations might seem strange. This makes us think more about what species and varieties really are and how they relate to each other.
finetuned: If species were considered to be distinct and stable varieties, it would be easy to see why their hybrids should often be as complexly marked in resemblance to the parents as are those of the well-known varieties; being blended by successive crossings, and other allied characters, as are the hybrids of the well-known varieties. But these facts would be puzzling if species were made independently, and varieties by secondary action.

The door at the end of the gallery opened, revealing Mr. Rochester, who emerged with a candle in hand after coming down from the upper floor. One of the ladies quickly approached him and grasped his arm; it was Miss Ingram. 

He responded with a hint of humor, saying, “But please don’t pull me down or strangle me,” as the Misses Eshton began to cling to him as well. Meanwhile, the two older women, dressed in large white wraps, were making their way toward him with an air of urgency. 

He may have seemed somewhat imposing at that moment, with his dark eyes flashing. Taking a moment to compose himself, he continued.

title: Jane Eyre
input:
I recalled everything quite clearly; the language, the look, and the tone felt momentarily refreshed. I found myself in the classroom where Adèle was drawing. I leaned over her to guide her pencil, and she glanced up, surprised. 

“What is it, Miss?” she asked. “Your fingers are trembling like a leaf, and your cheeks are red — so red, like cherries!” 

I quickly tried to push away the unpleasant thought I had been forming about Grace Poole; it was unsettling to me. When I compared myself to her, I noticed our differences. Bessie Leaven had mentioned that I was quite a lady, and there was truth to that—I recognized that I was indeed a lady. In that moment, I felt I appeared much better than I did when Bessie last saw me; I had more color, more fullness, and a greater sense of vitality and enthusiasm, likely due to my brighter hopes and more profound joys.

“Qu’avez-vous, mademoiselle?” said she. “Vos doigts tremblent comme la feuille, et vos joues sont rouges: mais, rouges comme des cerises!”

I hastened to drive from my mind the hateful notion I had been conceiving respecting Grace Poole; it disgusted me. I compared myself with her, and found we were different. Bessie Leaven had said I was quite a lady; and she spoke truth - I was a lady. And now I looked much better than I did when Bessie saw me; I had more colour and more flesh, more life, more vivacity, because I had brighter hopes and keener enjoyments.
